Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is seeking a GIS Analyst to support our Mapping & Analysis team in our Austin, TX office. The selected candidate would join a team of more than 2000 environmental professionals across the U.S. Through our Earth & Environment Division, WSP provides planning, permitting, engineering, site assessment and corrective action services to clients worldwide. Across multiple industries, our diverse staff specializes in the areas of siting/routing, air, water, waste, ecological and cultural resources throughout our many offices located across the country and internationally.

Your Impact

Provide mapping and analysis support for routing and siting, impact assessment, and analysis for natural gas pipelines and high voltage electric transmission lines.
Pprovide support for projects including:
Spatial data collection
Evaluation
Compilation
Creation
Conversion
Cuerying
Processing
Analysis
cartographic design and map production

Perform practical Geodatabase design, creation, and maintenance; compile metadata and data documentation; and provide technical support for coordinate/projection on information and related issues.
Assist technical staff and project managers by offering input and analysis with low-level threat mitigation activities, master planning, and permitting activities.
Work with cross-functional teams, CADD, and other technicians in executing project work.
Complete training on assigned tasks.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Education/Experience

Bachelor's degree in GIS, Geography, Landscape Architecture, Planning, Environmental Resource Management, or related field with a specialization in GIS
1 to 3 years professional experience with ArcGIS
Consulting experience with linear utility routing and siting projects
Experience providing GIS analysis for a State and/or Federal environmental process
Trimble GPS data collection & Processing Software
Presentation-quality cartographic skills (portfolio examples are welcome)
Analytical skills and prior experience with research techniques, modeling data, scanning and digitizing files, and experience maintaining records and databases with assigned projects required.
Competent interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to a scientific and non-scientific audience.
Competent self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Candidate should be a self-starter with the desire and ability to take the lead on a task and possess the ability to handle multiple projects simultaneously.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision, as well as part of a team to meet business objectives.
Basic proficiency with business writing, office automation and communication software, web mapping applications and tools.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.
Strong general computer skills (troubleshooting/problem solving)
Proficiency in Windows OS and Microsoft Office Suite
Strong attention to detail

Preferred Education/Experience

ArcPro experience
AutoCAD or Microstation experience
ArcGIS Online Experience

About WSP

ABOUT US

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. Dedicated to serving local communities, we are engineers, planners, technical experts, strategic advisors and construction management professionals. WSP USA designs lasting solutions in the buildings, transportation, energy, water and environment markets. With more than 15,000 employees in over 300 offices across the U.S., we partner with our clients to help communities prosper.

www.wsp.com

Employees are also afforded a comprehensive suite of benefits including medical, dental, vision, disability, life, and retirement savings focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career.

At WSP, we want to give our employees the challenges they seek to grow their careers and knowledge base. Your daily contributions to your team will be essential in meeting client objectives, goals and challenges. Are you ready to get started?

This opportunity resides with All-Domain Operations (ADO)
, a business group within HII’s Mission Technologies division. All-Domain Operations comprises multi-domain operations, platforms and logistics, and intelligence operations.

HII designs, develops, integrates and manages the sensors, systems and other assets necessary to support integrated ISR operations and accelerated decision-making. With data fusion and mission management capabilities for the Department of Defense, the combatant commands and the intelligence community, HII advances the mission around the globe.

Leadership Mindset at HII – Mission Technologies

Role

Leadership at HII is a mindset, not a title. Through our Leadership Capability Framework, we define how every employee grows, leads, and contributes—regardless of role. It sets the standard for how you can develop yourself and what you can expect from leaders across our organization. We look for candidates who want to grow in alignment with these capabilities:

Know & Grow Your People – Commit to learning and supporting team success.
Build Relationships – Communicate openly, collaborate well, and build trust.
Take Ownership – Deliver on commitments and take pride in your work.
Customer First – Focus on the mission and those we serve.
Shape the Future – Bring ideas, curiosity, and continuous improvement.
Act with Urgency – Take initiative and follow through with purpose.

These capabilities guide how all employees contribute to our shared success across Mission Technologies.

Summary

The Geo-Spatial Analyst supports HII Mission Technologies by delivering precise, high quality geospatial products and analysis that enhance mission readiness and decision-making for defense, intelligence, and national security customers. This role develops and analyzes geo-spatial solutions using global imagery and vector data, advancing HII’s commitment to providing trusted, data-driven capabilities for complex operational environments.

What You Will Do

Design, analyze, and develop geo spatial solutions and product specifications that support mission objectives across global operational domains.
Conduct GIS analyses on natural resources and geospatial datasets to inform planning, operations, and intelligence activities.
Plan, design, develop, document, and analyze spatial and relational databases supporting customer and mission requirements.
Apply GIS tools and analytical software to manage spatial and tabular datasets used by mission partners.
Build geospatial databases by capturing and digitizing map information to support intelligence and operational modeling.
Produce mission-ready map products and visualizations that clearly represent geospatial datasets and analytic findings.
Identify, locate, and evaluate geospatial data sources to ensure accuracy, reliability, and mission applicability.
Conduct quality control and assurance of geospatial datasets to maintain high analytic standards and data integrity.
Perform research and develop analytical reports that leverage geospatial information for mission planning and decision support.
Conduct peer reviews to maintain accuracy and consistency across geospatial analyses and deliverables.
Support data ingestion, quality control processes, issue resolution, and documentation to improve workflow efficiency.
Maintain and update process documentation, data standards, and report templates aligned with HII quality expectations.
Generate maps, geospatial visualizations, and supporting materials for briefings, presentations, and mission reports.

What We Are Looking For

5 years relevant experience with Bachelors in related field; 3 years relevant experience with Masters in related field; 0 years experience with PhD or Juris Doctorate in related field; or High School Diploma or equivalent and 9 years relevant experience.
Experience using JIRA, Confluence, or comparable Agile workflow systems.
Understanding of automation processes and workflows for data ingestion and transformation.
Strong data analysis skills, including Excel functions such as PivotTables, formatting and standardization, and formula creation.
Ability to generate and review maps and geospatial materials for use in presentations and other visual products.
Experience with generation and review of analytical presentations and reports
Minimum of 3 years of experience with ArcGIS Pro base functionality.
Minimum of 2 years of experience working in an Agile environment.

Preferred: Bonus Points For...

Experience with ESRI tools and platforms.
Background in quality control processes, including schema compliance review and report quality oversight.
Familiarity with AWS data storage, processing, and retrieval workflows.
Knowledge of maritime data sets and related geospatial considerations.
Experience with ArcGIS Pro extensions.
Experience with Python / R / other data analysis tools.

Physical Requirements

May require working in an office, industrial, shipboard, or laboratory environment. Capable of climbing ladders and tolerating confined spaces and extreme temperature variances.

The listed salary range for this role is intended as a good faith estimate based on the role's location, expectations, and responsibilities. When extending an offer, HII's Mission Technologies division takes a variety of factors into consideration which include, but are not limited to, the role's function and a candidate's education or training, work experience, and key skills.

Meet HII’s Mission Technologies Division

Our team of more than 7,000 professionals worldwide delivers all-domain expertise and advanced technologies in service of mission partners across the globe. Mission Technologies is leading the next evolution of national defense – the data evolution - by accelerating a breadth of national security solutions for government and commercial customers. Our capabilities range from C5ISR, AI and Big Data, cyber operations and synthetic training environments to fleet sustainment, environmental remediation and the largest family of unmanned underwater vehicles in every class. Find the role that’s right for you. Apply today. We look forward to meeting you.

Why HII

We build the world’s most powerful, survivable naval ships and defense technology solutions that safeguard our seas, sky, land, space and cyber. Our workforce includes skilled tradespeople; artificial intelligence, machine learning (AI/ML) experts; engineers; technologists; scientists; logistics experts; and business administration professionals.

Recognized as one of America’s top large company employers, we are a values and ethics driven organization that puts people’s safety and well-being first. Regardless of your role or where you serve, at HII, you’ll find a supportive and welcoming environment, competitive benefits, and valuable educational and training programs for continual career growth at every stage of your career.

Together we are working to ensure a future where everyone can be free and thrive.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, physical or mental disability, age, or veteran status or any other basis protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.title: Project Scientist, Natural Resources
jobs.description:
Application Requires a Cover Letter and Resume

RK&K is seeking a Project Scientist
to join our Natural Resources Team
in Baltimore. In this role you will be actively involved in a variety of wetland and forest delineation, permitting, habitat improvement, ecological restoration, protected species and other environmental projects, and will lead projects through a challenging regulatory environment by managing current projects, leading project teams, and collaborating with regulatory agencies and clients. You will work with a multidisciplinary RK&K team supporting transportation infrastructure, water resources, utilities, and site development projects in Maryland and throughout the Mid-Atlantic Region.

Essential Functions

Manage natural resources projects including all task deliverables, schedules, budgets, QA/QC reviews and internal and external coordination and communication to ensure successful project completion
Assist engineering teams with regulatory guidance, permitting strategies, technical writing, proposal development, construction environmental compliance, and oversight/management of environmental tasks for a variety of projects
Lead development of technical reports, Forest Stand Delineation and Forest Conservation Plans, wetland/stream documentation, and permit applications
Serve as field team lead for wetland delineations, forest assessments, tree inventories, mitigation site searches, protected species and other natural resource efforts
Mentor junior staff scientists and provide technical guidance to project teams
Facilitate meetings, develop presentation materials and present to project teams, clients, and agencies
Support business development and marketing
Participate in internal training and professional development, including safety, wetland and ecological training modules

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, or Natural Resources
5 to 7 years of relevant experience
Strong knowledge of federal and state environmental laws and regulations including Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, Endangered Species Act, Maryland Forest Conservation Act, Maryland Tidal and Nontidal Wetlands regulations, Maryland Chesapeake Bay Critical Area, and NEPA
GIS experience (ArcGIS preferred)
GPS field data collection Team-oriented but also able to work independently
Adept at juggling multiple tasks simultaneously
Organized, detail oriented, thorough and responsive
Excellent at written and verbal communication
Motivated to find creative solutions to environmental challenges
Excited to work outdoors in all seasons
Applications must include a cover letter and resume

Preferred Skills And Experience

Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Natural Resources or equivalent
At least one relevant professional credential such as Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), Certified Arborist (CA), Licensed Tree Expert (LTE), Geographic Information Systems Professional (GISP), Certified Wildlife Biologist (CWB), Certified Ecological Restoration Practitioner (CERP), Professional Engineer (PE), or similar
Restoration design experience - wetlands, living shorelines, streams, forests
CADD experience (Microstation or AutoCAD)
Experience conducting environmental fieldwork and permitting within Maryland, Delaware, DC, Pennsylvania, and Virginia
Develop proposals including scopes of work, fees, and preparation for client interviews

Work Environment

Mix of office, field, and remote work depending on project needs. Fieldwork may include walking long distances, in uneven terrain through natural environments including forests and wetlands, and exposure to hot, humid, cold, and wet weather conditions.

What We Offer

RK&K offers excellent career advancement opportunities and professional growth. We also offer attractive compensation packages commensurate with experience and a comprehensive benefits package including:

Hybrid work (home and office)
Paid time off
Tuition reimbursement (after one year of employment)
Health, dental, vision, life and disability insurances
Paid parental leave
Wellness programs and employee resource groups
Career development
Matching 401(k) plan
Paid holidays
Much, much more!

Why RK&K?

As a full-service engineering, construction management and environmental firm, RK&K provides the opportunity to work on projects in the communities where we live and work. With over 100 years of service, RK&K fosters a culture of collaboration, trust, and professional development. To its clients, the firm delivers concepts, processes, and outcomes that are designed for success, and we continually seek to maintain our reputation as a trusted partner, responsive employer, and community steward.

Design your career at RK&K, Apply Today!

Ensure that all field sampling, monitoring, inspections and data management are conducted in accordance with company requirements and in compliance with local, state, and federal regulations while continuously aligning daily functions to reflect Kinross’ values. This is a high-impact global role for an accomplished scientist or engineer who can move confidently between technical depth, strategic direction and practical implementation. Set the global environmental technology strategy across waste, wastewater, air emissions, vent treatment, recovery and recycling, informed by Best Available Techniques (BAT).
Identify, assess and mature emerging technologies, taking opportunities from laboratory and pilot-scale evidence through to robust manufacturing application.
Partner with global and local manufacturing teams to solve critical environmental challenges, improve site performance and safeguard license to operate.
Provide technical leadership and independent challenge for environmental projects, assessing feasibility, environmental benefit, risk, operability and cost.
Influence product and process choices early by evaluating waste streams, especially wastewater, during active-ingredient process development.
Develop practical, high-value solutions that reduce impacts to air, water and land across existing products and manufacturing sites.
Build and lead a connected global environmental technology community spanning Technology & Engineering, Production & Supply, Environmental Managers, process development teams and external experts.

Clear communication and stakeholder-influencing skills at all levels.
Experience working across multicultural, multinational teams, with a recognised record of technical delivery.

jobs.description:

Conservation Agriculture (Fixed-Term)

Organization

One Acre Fund

Posted 4 Sep 2026 Closing date 3 Dec 2026

About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

About The Role

We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.

Responsibilities

Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.
Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.
Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.
Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning.

Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption

Provide hands-on technical guidance to field teams delivering farmer trainings, workshops, Farmer Field Schools, and demonstration plots.
Build the capacity of field staff and local extension agents to effectively promote and support conservation agriculture adoption.
Provide timely agronomic troubleshooting to farmers and field teams addressing crop, soil, pest, and climate-related challenges.
Work with MEL and field teams to develop and implement systems that track adoption, farmer outcomes, and opportunities for scaling.

Agronomic Research, Practice Optimization & Impact

Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability.
Collaborate with R&D teams to design and oversee field assessments of soil health, crop performance, and environmental outcomes.
Analyze field evidence and farmer feedback to identify high-impact practices and recommend improvements to conservation agriculture programming.
Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models.

Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership

Build and manage strategic relationships with public, private, NGO, academic, and other technical partners supporting conservation agriculture initiatives.
Coordinate project plans, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and data sharing across internal teams and external consortium partners.
Represent the conservation agriculture program in technical discussions and ensure strong alignment between farmer needs, organizational priorities, and partner objectives.
Identify opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and resource mobilization that strengthen program quality, scale, and long-term impact.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Master’s degree in Agronomy, Agroecology, Crop Science, Soil Science, or a closely related agricultural field.
Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, conservation agriculture, regenerative agriculture, or agroecological farming systems.
Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder projects involving government, NGOs, research institutions, academia, or private-sector partners.
Strong hands-on experience working directly with smallholder farmers and field teams, with willingness to travel extensively and spend significant time in rural settings.
Proficiency in English is required; additional regional or international languages are an advantage.

Tetra Tech is looking for an Ecological Clerk of Works
to join Us in Shaping the Future of Ecological Delivery.
We have opportunities available across Scotland including Inverness, Edinburgh and Glasgow.

Join our collaborative Ecology team to support some of Scotland’s most exciting renewable energy, residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects. This is an opportunity to play a hands-on role in protecting biodiversity while helping clients deliver projects safely, compliantly, and efficiently. You’ll work within a technically strong, multi-disciplinary environment where your ecological expertise, practical judgment, and communication skills will make a visible impact on project outcomes.

Purpose & Scope of the Role

As an Ecological Clerk of Works, you will provide day-to-day ecological supervision and monitoring on large-scale construction and development sites across Scotland. You will help ensure ecological mitigation, protection measures, and site controls are implemented effectively, while supporting contractors, clients, and project teams with practical, proportionate solutions.

The role supports a wide range of ecological services for renewable energy, residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects, including onshore elements of major wind developments, as well as onshore wind and solar schemes. You will contribute to compliant project delivery by carrying out site inspections, supervising ecological surveys, maintaining accurate records, and responding to unexpected ecological issues on site.

Your Impact in This Position

You will help shape successful project delivery by protecting ecological interests while keeping works moving in a practical and compliant way. Your contribution will support regional and national project success, strengthen client confidence, and help maintain the organisation’s reputation for technical quality, innovation, and sustainable outcomes.

You will also play an important mentoring role, supporting junior ECoWs and technicians, sharing knowledge, and helping build capability within the wider ecology team.

Core Capabilities

Technical Expertise

Apply strong ecological knowledge and field-based experience to deliver effective site supervision, make sound decisions on site, and support protected species and mitigation requirements.

Project Management

Support the delivery of ecological works across small to medium scale projects, maintaining quality, managing priorities, and contributing to site reporting, compliance, and practical problem-solving.

Innovation

Use modern tools and progressive approaches to improve delivery, including digital data capture and mapping, and contribute to continuous improvement in ecological site practice.

Client Engagement

Build positive working relationships with clients, contractors, statutory bodies, and other stakeholders through clear communication, professionalism, and proactive site support.

Team Support and Development

Mentor junior colleagues where required, contribute to a collaborative team culture, and help support equipment, training, and knowledge-sharing activities.

Qualifications & Experience

Degree in Ecology, Environmental Science, or a related discipline
Associate membership of CIEEM, or ability to apply for membership
CSCS card
Full driving licence
Proven experience as an Ecological Clerk of Works, or in a similar ecological consultancy role
Strong practical field skills and good knowledge of UK wildlife legislation

Ability to work independently on site and make rapid, defensible decisions

Beneficial

NatureScot protected species licence

Experience supporting licensed works
GIS, mapping, or mobile data-capture experience

Working Environment

This is a site-based role working across Scotland, so you should expect regular travel and periods away from home. The role will involve working on construction and development sites, liaising with contractors and clients, and carrying out ecological supervision in changing site conditions.

You should be prepared for flexible working patterns aligned to project needs. A hybrid approach may be possible for non-site-based tasks, but the role will primarily require time on site and travel between project locations.

Tetra Tech is a leading provider of consulting and engineering services working across the full project lifecycle worldwide. jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

About The Role

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is seeking a Lead Business Analyst
to serve as the senior BA lead on a federal environmental data integration program. In this role, you will bring expertise in Endangered Species Act - Section 7 consultation processes and federal environmental platform workflows to drive requirements, compliance validation, and cross-agency coordination at the highest level.

Work Location:
Remote

Roles And Responsibilities

Serve as the senior business analysis lead across the full project, providing SME-level expertise in Endangered Species Act - Section 7 consultation processes, platform workflows, and multi-agency coordination
Lead requirements elicitation and documentation for all platform changes including species display, decision logic updates, template updates, and consultation routing
Conduct gap analysis between current platform capabilities and integration requirements, documenting findings for technical deliverables
Facilitate joint requirements workshops with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) Ecological Services and NOAA Fisheries SMEs
Lead the development of consultation logic alignment documentation for joint agency use
Support compliance validation by verifying that species list generation, decision logic, template content, and consultation routing meet regulatory requirements
Coordinate with government SMEs to obtain required approvals and sign-offs on compliance-critical deliverables
Lead pilot consultation workflow design, defining scenarios covering all consultation types
Analyze pilot results and live consultation feedback, translating findings into actionable system updates
Lead the development of the Pilot Report with Metrics, capturing consultation cycle times, completion rates, defect summaries, and actionable findings from pilot workflow execution
Lead the development of the Endangered Species Act - Section 7 Compliance Validation Checklist, documenting validation criteria for species list generation accuracy, decision logic correctness, template content completeness, and consultation routing
Coordinate government review and acceptance of Updated DKeys and Consultation Package Builder Assets, ensuring all content meets regulatory requirements and agency sign-off is obtained
Contribute to final operational documentation and year-end reporting

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

Bachelors degree and 10 years professional experience or a Masters degree and 8 years professional experience or an Associates degree and 12 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 16 years' professional experience.
U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance
Extensive years of business analysis experience on federal IT programs
Expertise in Endangered Species Act - Section 7 consultation processes
Experience with federal environmental regulatory systems and multi-agency coordination
Strong requirements elicitation, documentation, and stakeholder facilitation skills
Experience supporting compliance validation activities on federal programs
Experience capturing and reporting pilot metrics including cycle times, completion rates, and defect summaries
Experience facilitating OMB or executive-level government reviews and demonstration preparation

Preferred Qualifications

CBAP or equivalent BA certification preferred
Direct experience with the FWS Information for Planning and Consultation (IPaC) platform, Ecological Services, or NOAA Fisheries systems
Experience with DOI, FWS, or NOAA Fisheries programs
Familiarity with data migration or system integration projects in a federal context
Active Public Trust Clearance

Details

Target Salary Range: $86,000 - $138,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual's experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

Benefits Statement: Peraton offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, health savings account, short/long term disability, EAP, parental leave, 401(k), paid time off (PTO) for vacation, and company paid holidays. A full listing of available benefits can be viewed at https://www.careers.peraton.com/benefits.

However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. By applying to this job, you are expressing interest in the role and the Company. During the review of your application, you may be required to participate in an on-camera interview, as well as participate in a process to verify your identity. Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools of any kind during Peraton interviews is strictly prohibited unless the candidate has obtained prior written authorization. All interview responses must be the candidate's own.

jobs.title: Senior Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP is currently initiating a search for a Senior Environmental Scientist – Environmental Permitting & Compliance
to support our Earth & Environment Team in New York
. This position will support a diverse portfolio of energy, transportation, infrastructure, and development projects, with opportunities to work across environmental permitting, natural resources, and construction environmental compliance.

The successful candidate will be a versatile environmental professional with experience working in New York City and Long Island and comfortable supporting projects both in the field and in the office. Field responsibilities may include natural resource surveys, wetland delineations, environmental inspections, construction compliance monitoring, and coastal or marine field assignments. Office responsibilities may include preparation of environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, agency coordination materials, and environmental compliance documentation.

Your Impact

Conduct environmental field investigations, including wetland delineations, habitat assessments, natural resource surveys, and construction compliance inspections.
Support federal, state, and local environmental permitting for projects in New York City and Long Island.
Prepare environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, agency coordination materials, and compliance documentation.
Interpret permit conditions, environmental commitments, construction plans, and environmental specifications and communicate requirements to project teams and contractors.
Perform environmental inspections and construction compliance monitoring for energy, transportation, utility, infrastructure, and development projects.
Support coastal and marine environmental compliance activities, including field monitoring and coordination with construction contractors and environmental specialists, as needed.
Review construction work plans and method statements for activities occurring in or adjacent to environmentally sensitive resources.
Identify environmental compliance issues and work with project managers, contractors, and technical specialists to develop practical corrective actions.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, planners, environmental scientists, construction managers, regulatory specialists, and subcontractors.
Provide technical guidance and QA/QC oversight to junior environmental staff and field personnel.
Support multiple projects and assignments depending on project needs, including a combination of office-based technical work and field assignments.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
5 to 7 years of experience in environmental consulting, environmental permitting, natural resource assessment, and/or construction environmental compliance.
Experience working on environmental projects in New York City and/or Long Island, with familiarity with the region’s regulatory environment and infrastructure setting.
Experience conducting environmental fieldwork, which may include wetland delineations, natural resource surveys, construction monitoring, or environmental inspections.
Working knowledge of federal, state, and local environmental regulations and permitting requirements.
Experience preparing environmental permit applications, technical reports, impact evaluations, or similar environmental documentation.
Ability to interpret environmental permits, construction drawings, environmental specifications, and regulatory requirements.
Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with project managers, contractors, field crews, clients, and regulatory agencies.
Ability to work independently in the field while also collaborating effectively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify environmental risks and recommend practical solutions.
Ability and willingness to work in a variety of field conditions, including construction sites, wetlands, coastal environments, and potentially vessel-based settings.
Ability to travel throughout New York City, Long Island, and the surrounding region based on project needs.
Proven commitment to workplace health and safety and compliance with WSP health, safety, drug/alcohol, and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Occasional travel may be required depending on project-specific requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Environmental Science, Ecology, Biology, Natural Resources, or a related discipline.
Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS) certification or progress toward certification.
Experience with environmental permitting and agency coordination involving NYSDEC, USACE, NYC agencies, Nassau County, Suffolk County, and other applicable local regulatory authorities.
Familiarity with wetland, waterway, coastal, and natural resource permitting requirements applicable to New York City and Long Island.
Experience supporting energy, utility, transportation, infrastructure, or development projects in the New York metropolitan area.
Experience with coastal or marine environmental compliance and monitoring.
Experience leading field teams or providing technical oversight to junior staff.
40-Hour OSHA HAZWOPER training (29 CFR 1910.120) preferred.
Basic First Aid and Adult CPR training desired.

WSP Benefits:

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on a providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Compensation:

Expected Salary (all locations): $100,000 - $130,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and offer for this position, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

**About the engagement**  
A state regulatory agency needs a spatial analysis of licensed delivery operations in a regulated market: where delivery service exists, where it does not, and which populations sit outside any current service area. The agency will use the resulting map to evaluate service area expansion requests and to identify underserved geography. The product becomes a standing tool the agency maintains after the engagement ends.

**What you would do**

* Geocode and validate licensed operator and delivery asset location data provided by the client
* Build service area layers using defensible assumptions, including drive\-time isochrones rather than simple radius buffers
* Overlay coverage against population, density, and relevant demographic geography to identify and quantify service gaps
* Produce an interactive web map that agency staff can use without desktop GIS software or a paid license
* Produce static, print\-quality map exhibits suitable for a report submitted to a state legislature
* Document data sources, projections, service area assumptions, and update procedures so agency staff can refresh the map in future cycles
* Deliver clean project files and layers in a format the client retains

**Required**

* Three or more years of applied GIS work with a portfolio of finished maps
* Proficiency with ArcGIS Pro or QGIS, and comfort producing web\-deliverable output (ArcGIS Online, Leaflet, Mapbox, Felt, or comparable)
* Geocoding and address validation experience with messy administrative data
* Network or drive\-time service area analysis experience
* Strong cartographic judgment. Output will be read by policymakers, not analysts
* Ability to document methods clearly enough for someone else to reproduce them
* Availability to deliver against fixed dates in November and December

**Preferred**

* Bachelor's or master's in geography, GIS, urban planning, public health, or a related field
* Experience with public sector or regulatory clients
* Python scripting for geoprocessing automation
* Experience with accessibility or service coverage analysis in any sector, including health care, transit, food access, or broadband

The Global Green Growth Institute (GGGI), through funding from the Climate Technology Accelerator Fund (CTAF), is implementing the project “AI-Powered Satellite Platform for Climate Risk & Renewable Energy Mapping in Paraguay”. The project aims to strengthen climate resilience and renewable energy planning through the development and demonstration of an AI-enabled geospatial platform integrating satellite-derived renewable energy resource mapping, climate risk analytics, and decision-support tools.

Paraguay's electricity sector remains highly dependent on hydropower, which increases vulnerability to climate-induced droughts and hydrological variability. At the same time, the country has significant untapped solar and wind energy potential, particularly in the Chaco region. However, the lack of high-resolution geospatial information limits evidence-based planning and investment decision-making. The project will address this gap by generating solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability datasets and demonstrating an interoperable geospatial platform to support government institutions, academia, and other stakeholders in advancing the country’s renewable energy matrix diversification.

Key Objectives Include

Develop and validate high-resolution renewable energy and climate risk maps.
Support the deployment of a prototype web-based geospatial platform.
Strengthen institutional and technical capacity in the use of geospatial tools for climate and energy planning.
Support stakeholder engagement, validation, and scale-up planning.
Generate evidence for future replication and investment opportunities in Paraguay and the wider Gran Chaco region.

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The Geographic Information System (GIS) and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will provide technical support for the collection, processing, analysis, validation, visualization and reporting of geospatial data required for the implementation of the CTAF project.

The key tasks of this consultant position are as follows:

Collect, organize, and assess spatial datasets from government institutions and public sources.
Conduct GIS processing and spatial analysis using appropriate software and methodologies.
Develop and validate renewable energy resource mapping products, including geospatial analyses to support renewable energy planning and investment decision-making. Generate, analyze, and validate climate-risk layers, including drought and flood-related information, and develop decision-support products for national stakeholders. Prepare geospatial databases, metadata, and cartographic products.
Support testing and validation of spatial data integrated into the project platform.
Participate in stakeholder consultations, deliver training sessions, and technical meetings.
Contribute to the preparation of reports, presentations, and technical documentation.
Provide recommendations for data management, interoperability, and future scale-up of the platform.
Liaise with relevant stakeholders to ensure alignment of information generated and interoperability with the systems in place.
Serve as the national geospatial specialist and coordinate technical aspects with the consulting firm responsible for system deployment, ensuring the quality, consistency, and integration of geospatial datasets and analytical outputs.
Provide technical review and quality assurance of datasets, platform components, metadata, and interoperability mechanisms delivered by the consulting firm responsible for developing the platform.
Support validation of platform integration requirements and future interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM.

SCOPE OF WORK

The GIS and Geospatial Data Specialist Consultant will be part of the project implementation team and will work under the direct supervision of the CTAF Project Manager at GGGI Paraguay and in close coordination with national counterparts.

The consultancy is expected to deliver the following key results:

Geospatial Data Assessment and Coordination Report: Compile, review, organize and assess national geospatial datasets availability, quality, accessibility, and suitability related to renewable energy resources, climate risks, topography, infrastructure, and environmental information. Develop metadata catalogue and geospatial database inventory. Identify technical requirements and recommendations to facilitate interoperability with MADES information systems, including SIAM, and coordinate with consulting firm.
Technical Review and Validation of Climate and Renewable Energy GIS Dataset Package: Review and validate generation, processing, integration, quality control, accuracy, and validation of solar, wind, drought, flood, and climate-energy suitability layers. Support quality assurance and consistency checks of geospatial datasets developed under the project. Prepare technical documentation and metadata.
GIS Platform Support and Validation Report: Support data preparation, testing, visualization, validation, and demonstration of geospatial layers within the prototype web-GIS platform. Assess compliance with national data management requirements and interoperability standards. Review repository structures, metadata management procedures, and data-sharing mechanisms. Document validation results and recommendations for SIAM Integration.
Capacity Building and Final Technical Report: Deliver technical support for workshops and stakeholder consultations. Participate in technology-transfer activities conducted by the consulting firm. Support knowledge transfer and institutional capacity-building activities with designated MADES personnel. Review training materials, user guidance documents, lessons learned, and final consultancy report summarizing all activities undertaken during the consultancy.
The Consultant must integrate the comments of GGGI, and the technical focal points of other institutions involved, within 5 days after receiving the comments or requests for revision of the deliverables. All reports will be produced in Spanish and English and will follow GGGI's format requirements and will be submitted along with full raw data sets, research materials, minutes, interviews, and participant listings. Executive summaries will be delivered in English, and the final consolidated product of the consultancy must include a full English translation.

REPORTING ARRENGEMENTS

During the first week of assignment the consultant will define the reporting arrangements of the consultancy, in consultation with the national counterpart and the Project Manager. The consultant shall provide his/her own computer equipment and maintain access to ArcGIS Pro and any other software required to successfully perform the assignment.

Payments will be made against delivery of the products with prior approval from MADES, and approval from the GGGI Project Manager.

The consultant is expected to work in close coordination with MADES and other relevant institutions and may be required to work from MADES offices or other locations designated by the Project Manager.

Qualifications/Experience/Knowledge

Academic Qualifications

Master's degree in Geography, Geomatics, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Environmental Sciences, Engineering, Natural Resources Management, or a related field; or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

Professional Experience

Minimum 5-8 years of professional experience (preferred 7) in GIS, spatial analysis, or geospatial data management.
Demonstrated participation in at least 5 projects involving geospatial analysis and mapping, preferably related to natural resources management, environmental monitoring, climate change, land use planning, energy, or infrastructure.
Demonstrated experience in at least 3 projects involving integration, management, or development of geospatial databases and metadata systems, remote sensing, Earth observation, or satellite imagery processing.
Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects involving climate risk analysis, environmental assessment, disaster risk management, or related fields.
Demonstrated experience in at least 2 projects implemented with government institutions, international organizations, development partners, or public-sector entities.
Demonstrated experience in geospatial database management, metadata development, and spatial data governance, preparing technical maps, reports, and geospatial products for decision-making.
Experience working in Paraguay or in the Latin America and Caribbean region.

The Following Will Be Considered Assets

Experience in renewable energy resource assessment, solar and/or wind potential mapping, renewable energy suitability analysis, or GIS-based energy planning.
Experience in web-GIS platforms, spatial data portals, online dashboards, or geospatial visualization tools.
Experience delivering capacity-building, technical training, or knowledge-transfer activities related to GIS and remote sensing.
Experience using Google Earth Engine (GEE), Python, or other tools for geospatial analysis and remote sensing applications.

Skills and Knowledge

Strong analytical and cartographic skills.
Knowledge of spatial data management and metadata standards.
Demonstrated proficiency in ArcGIS Pro for geospatial analysis, geodatabase management, metadata development, and cartographic production.
Ability to communicate technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Strong report writing and presentation skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken, is a mandatory requirement, as the consultant will be required to conduct meetings, prepare deliverables, and communicate with international stakeholders in English.

About The Company

Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills.

Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer.

Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it.

Safe: We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities.
Committed to Serve: We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations.
Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment.
Driven: We deliver results in the right way.
Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person.

We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods.

Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets.

We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation.

With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers.

Recycling and Waste

We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs.

Environmental Solutions

Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need.

Sustainability Innovation

Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth.

The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America.

Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year).

jobs.description:
Wilson & Company, Inc., Engineers & Architects, a national multi-disciplined engineering and architecture consulting firm, is currently seeking a full-time Environmental Professional – Biologist and Wetland Specialist to join our Rocky Mountain Region team in one of our offices in Utah or Colorado. You’ll join our growing team of environmental professionals from across the company to perform biological surveys, wetland delineations, draft reports and site forms, conduct environmental analyses, and deliver quality documents supporting our federal, state, local, and tribal clients under the Clean Water Act (CWA), the Endangered Species Act (ESA), the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and other applicable federal and state regulations for environmental resource management.

In this position, you will perform fieldwork, evaluate potential environmental impacts and mitigation requirements, and write technical reports for wetland and biological resources on a variety of transportation, railroad, land development, and stormwater/wastewater projects. Biological resources include, but are not limited to, wetland delineation and mitigation, threatened and endangered species, wildlife, vegetation, noxious weeds, and environmental permitting. Aside from biological resources, we will also have you assist in compliance with NEPA and other environmental laws. Strong writing skills are required and experience with GIS is preferred. For the right candidate, this position has the potential to provide rapid growth.

All Wilson & Company environmental staff work collaboratively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across the firm to meet project goals, and with other key staff to build relationships both locally and in all states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work. Strong communication skills are required.

Essential Job Functions

Serve as project and/or task manager for environmental/NEPA projects in Rocky Mountain Region and firmwide; coordinate with and support others for overall project performance and deliver projects to clients on schedule and on budget.
Support the national environmental program through marketing, proposal preparation, and environmental analysis and documentation.
Work collaboratively and communicate effectively with engineering professionals in a variety of disciplines across Wilson & Company to meet project goals, and other key staff to build client relationships in the states where Wilson & Company is conducting environmental project work.
Provide technical environmental resource expertise for wetland and biological resources
Conduct fieldwork as it relates to project needs, includes travel throughout Colorado, Utah, and out-of-state travel to support a national environmental program.
Prepare biological resource reports, including Technical Memos, Biological Assessments, and Biological Evaluations.
Consult with jurisdictional and regulatory agencies and other stakeholders, including the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, etc.
Collaborate on the preparation of environmental and NEPA documentation, in part or in whole, including resource-specific technical reports, EIDs, CEs, EAs, and EISs.
Plan and conduct field delineations of Waters of the U.S., including wetlands, and conduct stream assessments.
Prepare delineation reports, functional assessments, mitigation plans, and Jurisdictional Determinations (JD) requests.
Prepare permit applications under Sections 404/401 of the Clean Water Act and NPDES Section 402.
Coordinate with state, federal, and local regulatory agencies.
Conduct vegetation and species habitat surveys.
Complete database reviews and background research to support NEPA documents and prepare NEPA documentation.
Prepare Section 7 consultations with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Landscape Architecture, Environmental Sciences, Environmental Planning, or a related discipline; advanced degrees preferred
Experience managing environmental projects and supporting NEPA compliance efforts, including technical writing and preparation of environmental documentation, is preferred.
2+ years of experience conducting wetland delineations, threatened and endangered (T&E) species assessments, permitting, reporting, and mitigation planning utilizing the Arid West, Western Mountain, Great Plains, and/or Midwest Regional Supplements. Candidates with 5+ years of experience are strongly preferred.
Experience preparing wetland delineation reports, T&E assessment reports, Section 404 permit applications, and mitigation plans.
Strong field skills in wetland delineation and T&E assessments, including GPS data collection and ArcGIS/GIS applications.
Ability to identify wetlands, jurisdictional waters of the U.S., and associated soils, vegetation communities, wildlife species, and habitats common to the Intermountain West, Colorado, Utah, and Midwest regions.
Experience coordinating with federal, state, local, tribal, and regulatory agencies; Colorado permitting experience and familiarity with CDOT projects is preferred.
Professional certification as a Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT), Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS), or the ability to qualify for PWS certification is preferred.
Proven ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams, manage tasks and budgets, and deliver work on schedule.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ArcGIS.

Nuestra misión en Amazon es ser la empresa más centrada en el cliente de la Tierra, y nuestro galardonado equipo de Environmental Assurance and Protection (EAP) es una parte clave para lograr ese objetivo. Amazon es una de las marcas más reconocidas en el mundo porque distribuimos millones de productos a nuestros clientes. Hacer nuestro mejor esfuerzo por nuestros clientes es de donde obtenemos nuestra energía, y es por eso que encontrará que abordamos las cosas de manera diferente aquí.

Amazon tiene implementadas las medidas necesarias para garantizar que los trabajadores cuenten con asientos adecuados. Durante los periodos de descanso y comida, los empleados podrán tomar su descanso en el área de comedor donde se encuentran las sillas disponibles, o salir de las instalaciones de la Empresa si así lo desean.

Amazon está buscando un Waste Coordinator (Coordinador de residuos) para que actúe como representante ambiental designado para su sitio. El Waste Coordinator brinda apoyo en la ejecución y en la implementación de los programas relacionados con el manejo de residuos del equipo de cumplimiento Ambiental Global (EAP) de Amazon dentro de las instalaciones asignadas.

Key job responsibilities

Caracterización y determinación de los residuos, incluyendo su segregación apropiada, contención, etiquetado y preparación para su envío, de acuerdo a las normas Estatales y Federales de México.
Organización de las áreas de almacenamiento y manejo de residuos, de acuerdo a los requisitos regulatorios y políticas de Amazon aplicables.
Realizar auditorías exhaustivas y precisas para la mejora continua incluyendo pero no limitados a los sitios de disposición de residuos, kits antiderrame, insumos para el manejo de residuos, etc.
Priorizar y manejar múltiples tareas técnicas.
Atender la limpieza y manejo de pequeños derrames de sustancias químicas en las instalaciones de Amazon.
Participar en todas las investigaciones relacionadas con incidentes ambientales en el Sitio. Trabajar en conjunto con el MSEM para realizar investigaciones exhaustivas para prevenir la recurrencia de los incidentes.
Apoyar en todos los envíos de residuos, y organizar toda la documentación necesaria para asegurar el correcto manejo de los residuos (permisos de los proveedores, manifiestos, comprobantes de disposición final, bitácoras, etc).
Solicitar órdenes de compra para equipo, contenedores, etiquetas y otros suplementos para mantener niveles de Stock apropiados en el área de residuos.
Asegurar que los registros necesarios para asegurar el correcto manejo de los residuos son completados y mantenidos adecuadamente.
Coordinarse con los equipos de WHS, OPS, RME, y otros equipos de los sitios responsables del correcto manejo de las sustancias químicas peligrosas para el correcto manejo de los residuos peligrosos y de los residuos no peligrosos o de manejo especial.
Apoyar al Regional Environmental Manager en la preparación de la documentación necesaria para las categorizaciones como generadores de residuos peligrosos y no peligrosos, así como para cumplir con los requisitos de tiempo máximo de almacenamiento de los residuos peligrosos.
Apoyar en la identificación de tendencias y áreas de oportunidad para reducción de costos.
Ser un recurso para responder preguntas relacionados con el manejo de los residuos por parte de operaciones.
Apoyar a operaciones en las actividades que se consideren necesarias para garantizar la consecución de los objetivos del sitio.

Job Title:
Drone Pilot / Surveyor

Position Summary

The Drone Pilot / Surveyor is responsible for performing aerial data collection, mapping, surveying support, and construction documentation across utility-scale solar EPC projects. This position utilizes Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS), survey equipment, and specialized mapping software to collect accurate field data used to support engineering, estimating, construction, project controls, and site management.

Working within a fast-paced, self-perform EPC construction environment, the Drone Pilot / Surveyor will support projects throughout the construction lifecycle—from existing-condition and preconstruction surveys through earthwork, pile installation, electrical construction, progress tracking, quantity verification, and final project documentation.

The ideal candidate combines strong UAS flight capabilities with practical surveying and construction knowledge and understands how accurate, timely field data directly impacts the successful execution of large-scale solar projects.

Key Responsibilities

Plan and conduct UAS/drone flight operations across large utility-scale solar construction sites in accordance with FAA regulations, company procedures, and project requirements.
Collect high-resolution aerial imagery and survey data for mapping, topographic surveys, construction progress, inspections, and project documentation.
Perform photogrammetry and aerial mapping to produce Ortho mosaics, digital terrain models (DTMs), digital surface models (DSMs), point clouds, and other project deliverables.
Support site surveying activities utilizing GPS/GNSS, RTK, robotic total stations, and other survey equipment as required.
Establish, verify, and maintain survey control throughout the duration of construction.
Support construction layout and verification activities for roads, grading, drainage, equipment pads, pile locations, electrical infrastructure, substations, and other project components.
Perform existing-condition and preconstruction aerial surveys to document site conditions prior to mobilization and construction.
Conduct routine progress flights to document construction status and provide project teams with current aerial imagery.
Assist with earthwork quantity calculations, stockpile measurements, cut/fill analysis, and verification of completed work.
Support grading operations by providing accurate surface data and comparing existing conditions against design surfaces.
Provide survey and aerial data to support pile installation, tracker/racking construction, module installation, underground electrical systems, inverter/transformer locations, and other solar construction activities.
Compare collected field data against IFC drawings, design models, and project specifications to identify potential discrepancies.
Support quality control activities by documenting installed conditions and assisting with verification of completed construction.
Process and manage drone imagery and survey data using applicable photogrammetry, CAD, GIS, and mapping software.
Coordinate with Project Managers, Superintendents, Survey Managers, Engineers, Project Controls, and field personnel to determine survey and aerial data requirements.
Maintain accurate flight logs, survey records, field notes, control documentation, and project files.
Organize and maintain aerial imagery and survey data so information is readily accessible to project teams.
Identify potential site, design, or construction issues through review of aerial and survey data and communicate findings to project leadership.
Maintain UAS equipment, batteries, survey instruments, and associated technology in proper working condition.
Perform pre-flight inspections and evaluate weather, airspace, site conditions, and potential hazards prior to flight operations.
Ensure all UAS operations comply with FAA Part 107 requirements and applicable federal, state, local, client, and company requirements.
Coordinate flight activities with project safety and field leadership to ensure drone operations do not interfere with cranes, equipment, electrical work, or other construction activities.
Support multiple projects and travel between active construction sites based on project needs.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, GIS, or related technical discipline preferred.
Current FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate required.
Previous experience operating drones/UAS for surveying, mapping, engineering, or construction applications.
Working knowledge of surveying principles, coordinate systems, elevations, benchmarks, and construction layout.
Experience collecting and processing aerial imagery for photogrammetry and mapping applications.
Experience with GPS/GNSS and RTK survey equipment.
Ability to read and interpret civil plans, grading plans, site layouts, construction drawings, and specifications.
Understanding of survey control and the importance of horizontal and vertical accuracy in construction applications.
Strong computer and data-management skills.
Ability to work independently in large, active construction environments while coordinating effectively with field personnel.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and priorities across multiple projects.
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
Ability and willingness to travel extensively based on project requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience supporting utility-scale solar, renewable energy, heavy civil, power generation, or large-scale EPC construction projects.
Experience working for a self-perform EPC or heavy civil contractor.
Experience with DJI Enterprise, Trimble, Leica, Topcon, or similar professional UAS and survey equipment.
Experience with photogrammetry and mapping platforms such as Pix4D, DroneDeploy, Propeller, Trimble Business Center, or similar applications.
Working knowledge of AutoCAD, Civil 3D, GIS, or comparable design/mapping software.
Experience creating Ortho mosaics, point clouds, surface models, contour maps, and volumetric reports.
Experience performing cut/fill analysis and earthwork quantity verification.
Experience with Ground Control Points (GCPs), checkpoints, RTK/PPK workflows, and survey-grade drone mapping.
Familiarity with solar site grading, pile installation, tracker systems, access roads, drainage systems, underground electrical collection systems, substations, and related utility-scale solar construction.
Surveyor-in-Training (SIT/LSIT) certification or related surveying credentials are a plus but not required.

Physical & Travel Requirements

Ability to travel extensively and potentially remain near project sites for extended periods based on construction schedules.
Ability to work outdoors in varying weather and environmental conditions.
Ability to walk large utility-scale solar sites over rough and uneven terrain.
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods while performing field operations.
Ability to carry and set up drone, survey, GPS, and related field equipment.
Ability to work around heavy construction equipment while maintaining appropriate situational awareness.
Ability to wear all required personal protective equipment (PPE).
Must be able to travel by vehicle and air as required.
