About The Role

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good. Your impact This job opportunity is available at ANY location in the United States. Ideally, selected candidates will be near a JACOBS U.S. based office, but we intend to hire the "best" candidates. The Drone Pilot is responsible for planning, coordinating, and executing safe and accurate unmanned aircraft operations to support digital delivery, BIM/VDC, design, construction, commissioning, and facility documentation activities on large-scale data center and advanced manufacturing projects. This role captures reliable aerial imagery, video, mapping, LiDAR, photogrammetry, and other reality-capture data that enables teams to understand existing conditions, monitor progress, validate installed conditions, improve site logistics, and support digital twin and asset management initiatives. The successful candidate will possess strong knowledge of commercial UAS operations, FAA Part 107 requirements, flight planning, construction-site safety, photogrammetry, surveying fundamentals, and the production of useful, well-organized digital deliverables. The role requires close collaboration with project leadership, VDC, construction, design, design, surveying, safety, security, and client teams. Key Responsibilities UAS Flight Operations Plan and conduct commercial drone flights in accordance with FAA regulations, company policies, project requirements, and site-specific safety procedures. Maintain required pilot credentials, aircraft registrations, operating records, pre-flight documentation, and flight logs. Perform pre-flight inspections and verify aircraft, batteries, sensors, firmware, remote-controller settings, and data-storage capacity. Operate drones safely in active construction, industrial, and data center environments while maintaining situational awareness and required separation distances. Coordinate flight windows, airspace restrictions, site access, security requirements, and operational constraints with project stakeholders. Use appropriate visual observers, spotters, and site communication protocols when required. Respond appropriately to changing weather, site conditions, equipment issues, and other operational risks. Reality Capture & Data Acquisition Capture high-quality aerial imagery, video, 360-degree imagery, and other UAS data for design, construction, commissioning, and operational use cases. Develop repeatable flight plans and capture standards for progress documentation, quantity verification, site logistics, existing-condition documentation, and turnover verification. Collect nadir and oblique imagery suitable for photogrammetry, orthomosaics, 3D meshes, point clouds, digital elevation models, and topographic or volumetric analysis. Coordinate ground control points, checkpoints, survey control, and site reference information when required for accurate mapping and model production. Integrate drone data with terrestrial laser scanning, BIM models, GIS data, schedules, and digital twin platforms, and asset-information systems. Ensure captured data is complete, properly organized, and traceable to the project, location, date, flight, and applicable coordinate system, and meets project quality requirements for downstream processing and analysis. Data Processing & Deliverables Process and quality-check drone imagery and reality-capture data using approved software and project workflows. The Environmental Technician supports the environmental team in ensuring mining operations comply with local, state/provincial, federal, and company environmental regulations and permits. Support waste management, hazardous materials handling, spill response, sediment/erosion control, and remediation or rehabilitation activities.

Collaborate with operations, engineering, and other departments; support training of site personnel on environmental topics when needed.
Perform other related duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Qualifications

High school diploma required

0–2+ years of environmental fieldwork experience (mining, industrial, or natural resource sector experience is a strong asset). Entry-level candidates with relevant education and demonstrated field skills will be considered.

Valid driver’s license (Class G or equivalent); ability/willingness to operate 4WD vehicles and boats is required.

Strong attention to detail and accuracy in sampling, data collection, and record-keeping.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office (especially Excel); familiarity with environmental databases (e.g., MonitorPro or similar) is an asset.
Ability to work independently with minimal supervision and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Good written and verbal communication skills.
Physical ability to work outdoors in challenging weather and terrain, hike uneven ground, and lift moderate loads (e.g., 20–50 lbs / 10–25 kg) as required.

Knowledge of relevant mining environmental regulations and permits (preferred).
Prior mine-site or industrial facility experience (preferred).

Manage, maintain, and continuously improve the site’s EHS management systems, supporting alignment with applicable standards such as ISO 14001 and ISO 45001.

Manage relationships with external service providers, consultants, contractors, waste-management companies, equipment vendors, and relevant regulatory agencies.
Support regulatory inspections, insurance audits, customer assessments, and corporate EHS reviews, coordinating responses and corrective actions where required.
Promote employee participation in safety programs and foster a culture of personal accountability, hazard awareness, environmental responsibility, and continuous improvement.
Remain current with changes in EHS legislation, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and manufacturing best practices, communicating their potential impact to site leadership.
Collaborate with senior leadership to develop and execute EHS strategies aligned with the organization’s operational priorities and broader business objectives.

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Occupational Health and Safety, Environmental Engineering, Industrial Hygiene, or a related discipline is preferred.
Proven Environmental, Health and Safety experience, preferably within a manufacturing or industrial environment.

Strong working knowledge of OSHA requirements and applicable federal, state, and local environmental, health, and safety regulations.
Knowledge of environmental and occupational health and safety management standards, including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001, is highly desirable.
Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, managing, and continuously improving comprehensive EHS programs and management systems.
Experience conducting workplace inspections, compliance audits, job hazard analyses, risk assessments, and ergonomic evaluations.
Proven ability to lead accident, incident, and near-miss investigations, perform root-cause analysis, and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.
Experience developing and delivering engaging EHS training programs to employees, supervisors, managers, and contractors.
Strong understanding of emergency response planning, hazardous-material handling, waste management, environmental compliance, and workplace safety procedures.
Ability to interpret complex regulations and translate them into clear, practical policies, procedures, and operational controls.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with experience using EHS metrics and trend analysis to drive measurable performance improvements.
Excellent communication, organizational, influencing, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to engage effectively with employees and leaders across multiple departments.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain accurate documentation, and operate effectively within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
Professional EHS certification such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM), or an equivalent qualification is desirable.

jobs.title: UAV Platform Development Engineer
jobs.description:
About Kepler Aviation

Kepler Aviation is a composite aerospace manufacturer based in Duzce, Turkiye. We are starting a new development programme for high thrust-to-weight, rapid-response multirotor platforms for defence applications, and we are looking for one engineer to own that platform from concept to first flight.

About the Role

This is a hands-on development role, not a design office role. You will lay out the platform, size the propulsion, build it, integrate the flight controller, tune it, fly it, break it, and improve it. You will be the person who makes the aircraft fly.

You will not be doing this alone. Our composite manufacturing team builds your structures in house, our design team supports you on aerodynamics and structural analysis, and our machine park is on site. But the platform is yours.

What You Will Do
• Develop high thrust-to-weight multirotor airframes from concept layout through flight-worthy prototype
• Size and validate the electric propulsion chain: motor, propeller, ESC and battery matching, based on your own thrust stand measurements rather than catalogue figures
• Characterise short-duration high-power operation, current draw and thermal behaviour under aggressive duty cycles
• Integrate and configure flight control on PX4 or ArduPilot, including parameter tuning of high-agility airframes and custom modes where the stock firmware is not enough
• Build prototypes with your own hands: wiring, assembly, bench testing and debugging
• Plan and run flight tests, write test cards, collect and analyse flight logs, and turn the results into design changes
• Work with the composite team on structure, layup and integration
• Integrate payload, datalink, antennas and onboard compute
• Keep test operations safe and disciplined

Requirements
• Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Electrical and Electronics Engineering or a related field
• A demonstrable record of building and flying high thrust-to-weight multirotors. Send us videos, flight logs, build threads or competition results. We care more about what you have flown than where you studied
• Practical electric propulsion sizing backed by measurement, including use of a thrust and torque test stand
• Deep working knowledge of PX4 or ArduPilot, including tuning aggressive airframes and reading logs to diagnose problems
• Real build skills: soldering, wiring, harnessing, assembly, bench debugging
• Flight test experience, including honest post-incident log analysis
• 3D CAD proficiency (SolidWorks, Siemens NX, CATIA or equivalent)
• Technical English, reading and writing
• Based in Duzce or willing to relocate

Preferred
• FPV racing, drone competition or Teknofest background
• Control theory: state estimation, guidance laws, proportional navigation
• Embedded C or C++ and Python for test automation and log analysis
• Experience with high discharge rate lithium packs, battery management and thermal management
• Experience with composite structures
• Radio links, telemetry and antenna placement
• Onboard compute (NVIDIA Jetson, Raspberry Pi) and vision pipelines

What We Offer
• A greenfield programme where you own the platform end to end
• In-house composite manufacturing, machining and a growing machine park
• Dedicated propulsion test stand and a flight test area
• R&D operations based in a technology development zone
• Direct access to decision makers, short decision cycles

How to Apply
Send your CV in English to hr@kepler.aero with the subject line "UAV Platform Development Engineer". Include links to anything you have built and flown.

Provide field support for site inspections and construction oversight.

IN THE OFFICE

Georgia Power’s Environmental Affairs organization is seeking an Engineer or Specialist to join the Environmental Compliance Assurance team. This team supports Georgia Power’s Environmental Management System (EMS) and the sustainment and improvement of Enablon, Georgia Power’s Environmental Management Information System (EMIS).

This role is designed for a candidate with direct experience working with environmental regulations who also has a passion for business process improvement, data quality, user support, and technology. The successful candidate will partner with environmental subject matter experts, facility personnel, and consultants to help ensure environmental regulatory requirements are consistently executed across Georgia Power.

Key Responsibilities

These Key Responsibilities are shared by the entire Compliance Assurance team. Individual responsibilities and assignments will be made based on team needs and strengths of the successful candidate.

Environmental Management Information System Support

Support the day-to-day sustainment and continuous improvement of the Enablon Environmental Compliance Assurance platform.
Partner with environmental subject matter experts to maintain accurate and useful system content, including tasks, checklists, inspections, forms, reference materials, and related compliance data.
Provide front-line user support, troubleshoot issues, and coordinate escalated support with consultants to help resolve system or process concerns in a timely manner.
Develop and maintain job aids, user guidance, and training resources for Enablon users.
Support functional enhancements by understanding business requirements, coordinating user testing, and helping implement practical system improvements.
Use Enablon data to develop reports and dashboards, improve data quality, and support leadership reporting.

Environmental Management System and Compliance Assurance Support

Develop and maintain a practical understanding of Georgia Power operations and how environmental requirements apply across facilities, business units, and environmental programs.
Build effective working relationships with Environmental Affairs subject matter experts, facility personnel, and business partners to support consistent EMS implementation and compliance assurance practices.
Support continuous improvement of EMS processes, documentation, performance reporting, and communication materials used by Environmental Affairs and facility teams.
Assist the compliance assurance field team with program support, process coordination, data review, reporting, and follow-up activities as needed.
Coordinate and strengthen the Environmental Affairs Training Program by helping organize training assignments, track completion, maintain training records, and develop or deliver EMS and Enablon-related training materials.
Support the Environmental Recordkeeping Program and help ensure environmental records remain aligned with Southern Company’s Records Information Management requirements.
Help translate business needs into clear process requirements, system improvements, reporting enhancements, user guidance, and training solutions.
Support the Company’s storm restoration and emergency response efforts as appropriate.
Up to 25% travel throughout the state of Georgia; occasional travel to Alabama will also be required.
These responsibilities represent the primary focus of the role; additional duties may be assigned based on business needs.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, environmental science, chemistry, biology, data science, management information systems, or a related field; equivalent relevant work experience may be considered.
Five or more years of relevant experience supporting environmental compliance programs, information systems, data/reporting processes, or related business processes.
Working knowledge of environmental regulatory programs such as air, water, waste, or related environmental media.
Experience supporting, implementing, improving, or administering business systems, information systems, or technology-enabled processes.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with environmental, health, and safety information systems such as Enablon.
Experience developing reports, dashboards, metrics, or data visualizations using Power BI or similar tools.
Experience providing user support, customer support, training, change management, or process adoption support.
Experience coordinating projects, system enhancements, testing activities, training initiatives, or cross-functional process improvements.

Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to build trust, influence outcomes, and work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to communicate complex environmental, system, and process information clearly through presentations, written guidance, training materials, and one-on-one support.
Sound judgment, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate alternatives, recommend practical solutions, and follow through on commitments.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Ability to build and maintain effective working relationships across Environmental Affairs, facility teams, business partners, vendors, and internal support organizations.
Ability to manage multiple assignments, competing priorities, deadlines, stakeholders, and follow-up items with strong attention to detail.
Ability to work through others, coordinate across teams, and help move work forward without direct authority.
Ability to support Environmental Affairs and Compliance Assurance goals as a collaborative, dependable, and solutions-oriented team member.

Other Attributes

Consistently demonstrates Our Values: Safety First, Intentional Inclusion, Act with Integrity, and Superior Performance.
Models ethical conduct and maintains a strong commitment to compliance, accountability, and professional behavior.
Takes initiative, follows through on commitments, and is comfortable making recommendations in ambiguous or evolving situations.
Adapts to changing business needs, stakeholder expectations, regulatory requirements, and system priorities.
Identifies practical solutions that balance compliance requirements, business needs, user experience, and long-term sustainability.
Maintains a high level of accuracy, organization, and attention to detail when following processes, reviewing data, and documenting work.

.

Dudek is currently seeking a full-time Environmental Technician I to join our team. The successful candidate will help Dudek on a wide variety of projects involving sensitive aquatic resources with a focus on implementation support for aquatic/water quality testing, analysis, management, invasive species control and invasive species permitting. Leads field and laboratory efforts, and ensures data is collected per appropriate methods and procedures
Experience, ability and aptitude to collect clear and accurate data and field notes

Ability to organize field or laboratory information into client-work products with direction from experienced staff
Participates in training efforts for data collection and analysis, including active participation in feedback for improvements
Evaluates and analyzes data with guidance from experienced staff
Collects or assists with the collection of water quality, environmental toxicology, biology, soil, and air quality data
Safely and correctly operates and maintains field data collection equipment
Communicates results of activities in written, oral, and graphical formats
Maintains inventory and assists with acquisition of laboratory supplies
Assists with scheduling laboratory and field data collection efforts
Leads and participates in construction and upkeep of field monitoring tools

Minimum Qualifications

Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in environmental science or a related field and/or relevant experience.
Knowledge and understanding of field and data analysis techniques related to aquatic environments
Strong data collection skills related to best practices, standard safety operating procedures, regulatory guidance
Strong written and oral communication skills
Willingness to travel for work, including overnight stays in hotels
Ability to safely drive/operate a vehicle to/from and around field work sites during daytime and nighttime hours
Must possess a valid driver’s license and have active personal automobile liability insurance by first day of employment

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of experience in a similar position in related discipline or setting
Familiarity with aquatic invasive species
Knowledge of California aquatic resource types and systems
Experience with aquatic invertebrates and microscopy
Comfortable using hand tools
General knowledge of California regulatory environment
Strong customer service emphasis and solution-oriented project delivery approach
Conscientious and detail-oriented with demonstrated accuracy and attention to detail

Ability to apply common sensed understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral or diagram form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.

jobs.description:
About Peraton

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world's leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we're keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Program Overview

The program is an IDIQ contract for an AWS-based cloud hosting system. Currently, Peraton is supporting the Cloud Security, IoT, and AIML use cases for the environment in a hybrid work environment with Federal employees. Peraton also support the following applications as part of the environment: Dremio, Tableau, Globus, Posit/RStudio, Atlassian, ThingLogix, Alteryx and CloudCheckr.

About The Role

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is looking for a Business Analyst
with expertise in the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), part of the Department of the Interior, which manages fish, wildlife, and habitats across the United States, Ecological Services business processes to serve as the dedicated FWS liaison on a federal data integration program. You will bridge the gap between the Peraton delivery team and FWS stakeholders, ensuring all platform changes meet FWS standards and obtaining required government approvals.

Work Location:
Remote

Roles And Responsibilities

Serve as the dedicated SME for FWS Ecological Services business processes, requirements, and stakeholder coordination
Document current-state FWS consultation workflows, decision logic structures, and template formats
Elicit and document FWS-specific requirements for species integration, including display standards, habitat designation presentation, and consultation routing rules
Coordinate with FWS ES staff to obtain the Range Mapping SOP and ensure all map production activities comply with SOP requirements
Facilitate iterative range map review cycles with FWS Ecological Services SMEs and coordinate FWS ES sign-off on deliverables
Support FWS ES review of platform UI and logic updates, demonstration materials, and compliance validation checklists
Coordinate FWS ES review and acceptance of updated decision logic and consultation package assets
Support FWS ES establishment of training completion metric targets
Serve as the primary liaison between the Peraton team and FWS Ecological Services

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

Bachelors degree and 8 years professional experience or a Masters degree and 6 years professional experience or an Associates degree and 10 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 14 years' professional experience.
U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance
Demonstrated years of experience in business analysis or program support on federal environmental programs
Strong understanding of ESA Section 7 consultation processes and FWS Range Mapping standards
Experience facilitating government stakeholder reviews and obtaining formal approvals
Excellent written communication skills; experience producing government-facing documentation

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience working with or supporting FWS Ecological Services operations
Direct experience with the IPaC platform or FWS Ecological Services IT systems
Experience coordinating multi-agency deliverable approvals (FWS + NOAA Fisheries)
Familiarity with DOI IT governance and FITARA compliance requirements
CBAP or equivalent BA certification
Active Public Trust Clearance

We are looking for candidates with 6 to 10+ years of experience in environmental engineering design and construction support. You’ll work on a variety of projects involving sediment remediation, stream and wetland restoration, and other in-water and upland environmental efforts. This role offers hands-on experience in site investigation, design development, and construction oversight, with opportunities to collaborate across disciplines and make a meaningful impact. Work may require travel within the northeast region, and occasionally elsewhere in the United States.

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively, show initiative and attention to detail, and possess a strong interest in environmental engineering.

Support planning, design, and implementation of environmental remediation projects, including dredging, capping, stream restoration, and wetland construction.
Prepare engineering design documents, including drawings, specifications, cost estimates, and calculations.
Contribute to technical reports such as sampling and analysis plans, feasibility studies, and design documentation.
Perform environmental sampling of soil, sediment, and water sampling,
Provide field support for site inspections and construction oversight.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, scientists, planners, and biologists.

Ensure deliverables meet Anchor QEA’s quality standards.
Travel occasionally for fieldwork, site visits, and project meetings (primarily in Eastern NY and Western MA).

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Environmental, Civil, Coastal, or Geotechnical Engineering.

Experience with sediment remediation projects (such as dredging and capping) and stream or wetland restoration projects.
Strong technical writing and communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong problem-solving and critical thinking abilities.
Willingness to travel for field assignments and meetings.

Project experience with geotechnical engineering evaluations related to sediments are considered a plus.

You’ll work on a variety of projects involving sediment remediation, stream and wetland restoration, and other in-water and upland environmental efforts. This role offers hands-on experience in site investigation, design development, and construction oversight, with opportunities to collaborate across disciplines and make a meaningful impact. The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to work independently and collaboratively, show initiative and attention to detail, and possess a strong interest in environmental engineering.

Perform environmental sampling of soil, sediment, and water sampling,
Provide field support for site inspections and construction oversight.
Coordinate with multidisciplinary teams including engineers, scientists, planners, and biologists.
Participate in construction support activities, including reviewing contractor submittals and RFIs.
Ensure deliverables meet Anchor QEA’s quality standards.
Travel occasionally for fieldwork, site visits, and project meetings (primarily in Eastern NY and Western MA).

What Are We Looking For?

Ideal Candidates Will Have The Following

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Environmental, Civil, Coastal, or Geotechnical Engineering.
6–10 years of experience in environmental remediation, including investigation, design, and construction.
Experience with sediment remediation projects (such as dredging and capping) and stream or wetland restoration projects.
Strong technical writing and communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
Strong problem-solving and critical thinking abilities.
Willingness to travel for field assignments and meetings.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with contaminated sediment sites and in-water remediation.
Working knowledge of AutoCAD Civil 3D and GIS for site planning and design.
Professional Engineer (PE) licensure in MA or NY, or on track to obtain within 1-2 years.

What Can You Expect?

A collaborative work environment where we encourage everyone to bring their authentic self. We offer competitive compensation and benefits. Benefits detailed below.

Who Are We?

Anchor QEA provides environmental planning, science, and engineering consulting services with the mission of transforming our environment and communities with integrity and vibe. With more than 500 people in offices across the United States, our collective vision is to be an inclusive, sustainable, and growing environmental innovator making generational impacts. By embodying our core values, we strive to be our clients’ first choice for solving their most challenging problems and to be our employees’ reason to be excited about going to work each morning. On the business side, we not only provide reliable infrastructure for some of ByteDance’s largest-scale vector and full-text hybrid search workloads, but also deliver enterprise-grade cloud search services to external customers through Volcano Engine, helping businesses unlock growth through data. We embrace a pragmatic yet ambitious engineering culture: while continuously publishing innovative research at top-tier conferences such as VLDB and ICDE, we remain strongly focused on real-world impact and commercial adoption, building a comprehensive product portfolio that serves a wide range of search and AI use cases.
Our team brings together leading database researchers and exceptional engineers from around the world. Together, we will explore uncharted technical territory, define the data foundation for the AI era, and empower both ByteDance and enterprises across industries to achieve AI-driven transformation.

Responsibilities
- Develop and evolve our Elasticsearch/OpenSearch and Milvus products, building high-performance and scalable search and vector retrieval capabilities.
- Develop high-performance full-text and vector search, including hybrid search, filtered search, multi-vector search, and large-scale ANN retrieval.
- Optimize vector indexing and distributed retrieval across HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, RaBitQ, storage, caching, and I/O.
- Explore cloud-native Vector Lakebase architectures for scalable search over data lakes and object storage.

- B.S in Computer Science, AI, Machine Learning, or a related field.
- Strong software engineering skills in C++, Golang, Java, or Python.
- Experience with search engines, databases, storage systems, or distributed systems.

- Strong understanding of distributed systems and performance optimization.

Preferred Qualifications
- Deep experience with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Lucene, Milvus/Knowhere, or similar systems.
- Strong knowledge of full-text search and (multi)-vector indexing, including HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, or related ANN algorithms.
- 5 years experience optimizing billion-scale or larger vector retrieval for latency, throughput, recall, and cost.
- 5 years experience with cloud-native storage, compute-storage separation, object storage, or lakehouse/lakebase architectures.

GIS Specialist V

to serve as the senior geospatial authority for a major regional program. You will guide analytic approaches, oversee data publishing processes, and support the development of tools and applications that make regional data accessible and actionable.

Utilize Esri server/mobile products, QlikSense, Power BI, open‑source GIS tools, and image processing software including ERDAS and ENVI.

Manage regional data holdings and ensure data assets are properly published, documented, and discoverable.
Develop and manage data intake processes for diverse data formats and sources, ensuring alignment with data requirements.
Collaborate with internal and external workgroups to refine data publishing processes and ensure procedural completeness.
Build and maintain data portals that support public and client access to environmental and operational data.
Develop front‑end and back‑end interfaces for applications, integrating modeling results into final products.
Provide visualization, analytics, and informatics support using Qlik, R, Python, Jupyter, and Power BI across cloud and local environments.
Review team work products for compliance with cartographic and metadata standards.
Deliver training on GIS tools, data systems, and data management best practices.
Produce and maintain system architecture documentation as systems evolve.

BS/BA degree or equivalent.
Experience:
Minimum of 8 years of GIS industry experience.
Technical Skills:

Proficiency with the Esri suite of GIS products.
Working knowledge of SQL for spatial queries.

Experience with Python and R scripting.

Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Must be eligible to obtain and hold a Tier 4 Public Trust.

jobs.description:
Requisition Id 17035

Overview:

The Integrated Operations Support Division (IOSD) at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) seeks a Geographic Information Systems (GIS) Specialist to serve as the functional system administrator for ArcGIS Enterprise, and partners with IT staff and data owners across ORNL. The GIS Specialist is the primary point of contact for the enterprise GIS platform, fostering customer relationships by proactively identifying, implementing, and communicating continuous improvement efforts.

The GIS Specialist will build awareness of existing GIS capabilities, develop, and implement new tools and workflows, and support the vision, roadmap, standards, and governance for GIS across the Directorate. Supported functional areas include site, facility, and asset management, utilities distribution, logistics, environmental safety & health, strategic planning, construction, engineering, emergency management, and security.

Major Duties/Responsibilities:

Serve as the functional system administrator for ArcGIS Enterprise (Portal, Server, Data Store) and associated applications and datasets.
Design, develop, and maintain web maps, web applications, web scenes, dashboards, and mobile apps using ArcGIS Experience Builder, Dashboards, Survey123, and related tools.
Administer and optimize enterprise geodatabases, including SQL views, schema design, privileges, versioning, and replica management.
Support data interoperability efforts to integrate CAD, BIM, tabular, and other datasets into enterprise GIS; ensure correct coordinate systems and projections (including ORNL custom coordinates).
Develop and maintain Python scripts, Arcade expressions, attribute rules, and automated processes (including batch scripts and Windows Task Scheduler jobs).
Publish and manage map, feature, image, geoprocessing, and real-time (GeoEvent) services.
Implement and support offline GIS workflows, mobile field work, GPS-based data collection, and road network analysis (Network Analyst).
Maintain data governance, metadata standards, and documentation for Enterprise GIS assets.
Develop and maintain GIS platform documentation including Software Quality Assurance, Business Impact Analysis, Contingency Planning, System Security Plans, etc.
Work closely with managers, process owners, IT staff, and end users to understand requirements, prioritize enhancements, and implement system/process improvements.
Provide general troubleshooting and user support to both GIS technical staff and non-technical map users
Administer licensing and user accounts for desktop and server applications.
Coordinate software procurement, planning, installation and vendor relations and support including training, coordinating software demonstrations, benchmarking, etc.
Deliver ORNL’s mission by aligning behaviors, priorities, and interactions with our core values of Impact, Integrity, Teamwork, Safety, and Service. Promote equal opportunity by fostering a respectful workplace – in how we treat one another, work together, and measure success.

Basic Qualifications:

A BS/BA degree in GIS, geography, environmental science, environmental informatics, computer science, engineering, natural sciences, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of relevant GIS experience.
Proficient with ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Enterprise; capable of architecting, developing, and maintaining web maps and web applications from enterprise data.
Experience with GIS data analysis, data cleaning/curation, and integration of multiple data formats (including CAD).
Working knowledge of SQL and relational databases for GIS workflows.

Preferred Qualifications:

MS/MA degree in geography, GIS, environmental science, environmental informatics, computer science, engineering, natural sciences, or a related field.
Experience as a technical lead, system administrator, or architect for an enterprise GIS environment.
Experience working with facilities and operations organizations, city/county governments, or utilities.
Advanced experience with:
ArcGIS Experience Builder and Dashboards
Enterprise geodatabases (e.g., SQL Server) including versioning and replicas
ArcGIS Server and Portal administration
Network Analyst and road network management
GeoEvent Manager and real-time GIS

Experience integrating GIS with asset management systems (e.g., Octave EAM) or other enterprise business systems.
Experience with Python and/or Arcade for GIS automation, analysis, or business logic.
Background in software support or customer-facing technical roles, including training and documentation.
Ability to work collaboratively with a diverse group of stakeholders and contribute to team goals.
Strong prioritization, communication, problem-solving skills, and attention to detail.

Special Requirements:

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain an HSPD-12 PIV badge.

For employment at Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), a Real ID compliant form of identification will be required. Additionally, ORNL is subject to Department of Energy (DOE) access restrictions. All employees must also be able to obtain and maintain a federal Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) and Department of Energy (DOE) Order 473.1A, which requires a favorable post-employment background investigation.

To obtain this credential, new employees must successfully complete and pass a Federal Tier 1 background check investigation. This investigation includes a declaration of illegal drug activities, including use, supply, possession, or manufacture within the last year. This includes marijuana and cannabis derivatives, which are still considered illegal under federal law, regardless of state laws.

For Hybrid eligible positions:

This position is located in Oak Ridge, Tennessee and requires onsite presence. We offer a flexible work environment that supports both the organization and the employee. A hybrid/onsite working arrangement may be available with this position, which provides flexibility to work periodically from your home, while reporting onsite to the Oak Ridge, Tennessee location on a weekly and regular basis.

bout

Our team is made up of over 7,000 dedicated and innovative individuals! to join our Environmental, Health & Safety, Sustainability, and Air Quality (EHSSAQ) Practice in Livonia, MI. Prepare environmental compliance plans and site-specific environmental and health & safety procedures, including SPCC Plans, Slug Control Plans, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and RCRA Contingency Plans.

Prepare emissions calculations and regulatory reports, including SARA Tier II, TRI, and Annual Air Emissions Reports.

0–5 years of relevant experience; relevant internships, co-ops, academic projects, or other environmental experience are preferred.

Scope of Eligibility

Open to permanent employees in a competitive title who work in the Division of Remediation Management and meet the requirements below.

Description

Under the limited supervision of a supervisory official in a state department, institution, agency, or local government agency, performs complex technical or scientific work including field and office studies, surveys, inspections, or investigations associated with enforcement of environmental laws and/or regulations, and environmental review and control work, or organizes and carries out programs/projects designed to study and evaluate environmental impact of specific projects on the environment; organizes and develops tests and reports to assess environmental impacts on physical, natural, and/or human environments; investigates environmental complaints concerning projects; conducts contract, grant, and/or loan processing; may be required to function as a lead worker providing guidance to lower-level Environmental Specialists; does other related duties as required.

Specific to the Position

​
Positions 1, 2, 3 - Northern Field Operations:

This position will require the timely review of remedial action reports submitted by certified environmental contractors performing remediations of homeowner heating oil tanks and Licensed Site Remediation Professionals submitting remedial phase reports related to Educational Facilities and Child Care Centers . The technical reports are evaluated to determine compliance with soils and groundwater remediation standards. This position will require field inspections of sites including Educational Facilities and Child Care Centers, Remedial Action Permits, Unregulated Heating Oil Tank (UHOT) cases, and other environmental incidents/complaints.

Position 4 - Southern Field Operations:

This position will require the timely review of remedial action reports submitted by certified environmental contractors performing remediaitons of homeowner heating oil tanks. The technical reports are evaluated to determine if contaminated soils and groundwater are remediated to state standards. This position is mainly an office position, but may include field inspections when warranted.

Positions 5,6,7,8 - BSM:

Duties include managing publicly funded projects with other staff and supervisors in the bureau which includes coordinating site specific funding requests and invoice processing, access coordination, contractor oversight, scope of remedial work development, and scheduling. Additional responsibilities include technical evaluation of environmental data and remedy recommendations, community interaction, and cost recovery support. Fieldwork is a major part of the job responsibilities and includes site inspections, oversight of contractor's conducting construction activities. Staff are assigned a state vehicle, a mobile phone, and a laptop since much of the work week is spent in the field.

Positions 9 & 10 - BCM:

These positions requires a timely review of highly complex remedial reports, workplans, and other documents submitted by environmental professionals on behalf of the responsible parties. The technical reports are evaluated to determine if contaminated media such as soils and groundwater are investigated and remediated to state regulations and standards. Those meeting the standards are issued approvals, those that do not meet the state requirements standards are required to revise and continue remediation until the standards are met.

Position 11 - BEMSA

The critical duties for this position involve performing unknown source investigations in the BEMSA Site Assessment Unit (SA) to accomplish established goals & objectives while investigating and sampling sites identified as potential sources of contamination at IECs. SA staff must demonstrate a high level of competence in technical report writing, investigative skills and data presentation. The position performs PCS, PA and SI investigations. The position evaluates IEC sites, determines the location of potential sources of contamination, writes sampling workplans, secures funding and performs sampling of soil and groundwater to determine if a source of contamination exists. This position has NJEMs and FSE data entry responsibilities

Position 12 - BEMSA

The critical duties for this position in the Environmental Measurements unit include overseeing and conducting field sampling collecting ground water, surface water, sediment, soil, landfill gas, indoor air measurements through use of various field instruments and coordinating analytical work through contract laboratories. The work involves performing field sampling and overseeing contractors performing field sampling at various hazardous waste sites both commercial and residential. Health and Safety training is required and medical surveillance.

Positions 13 & 14 - Brownfields:

Duties and responsibilities include the coordination of brownfield investigation, remediation, and redevelopment for the office’s BDA Program, Hazardous Discharge Site Remediation Fund (HDSRF) Program, Landfill Redevelopment Program, and/or Brownfield Redevelopment Incentive Program (BRIP). Staff will review and inspect documents submitted to the Department by Licensed Site Remediation Professionals (LSRPs) to ensure the investigations and remediations are performed in accordance with regulatory and statutory requirements.

Preferred Skill Set

Positions 1, 2 & 3
Review of remedial phase reports related to Educational Facilities and Child Care Centers, Review of remedial action reports for Unregulated Heating Oil Tank (UHOT) cases, Field audits of UHOT contractors, Oversight of permits by rule (PBR) related to UHOT cases, Preparation of on-scene coordinator permits (OSC) and oversight of such, Inspection of Educational Facilities and Child Care Centers, Inspection of deed notices, with or without Remedial Action Permits.

Position 4
The candidate is expected to have experience in the review of remedial action reports for Unregulated Heating Oil Tank (UHOT) cases, including data entry into NJEMS and the processing of No Further Action letters.

Positions 5,6,7 & 8 
Ability to manage state contractors. Interpret scientific data and make recommendations. Knowledge of Vapor Intrusion, POETS, NERAS & Subsurface Contracts, Technical Requirements for Site Remediation, CERCLA and NCP. Ability to engage with residents. The individual should be OSHA 40 hour trained since this is primarily a field position.

Positions 9 &10 
Case managers are responsible for overseeing the investigation and cleanup of complex hazardous waste sites conducted by private responsible parties and other government agencies. Will perform administrative and technical reviews of all remediation documents related to the remediation of contaminated sites in accordance with the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, Liability Act, Resource, Conservation and Recovery Act, & the NJDEP Technical Requirements.

Position 11:
Ability to work with limited supervision while conducting unknown source investigations. Knowledge of NJDEP Field Sampling Procedures Manual, USEPA PA/SI guidance, USEPA HRS Scoring system, Technical Requirements for Site Remediation, and Remediation Standards. Ability interpret scientific data and make evaluations and recommendations for identifying sources of contamination. Knowledge of State Contract Management, FSE and NJEMS procedures.

Position 12:
Ability to conduct environmental sampling, prepare data summary reports, and perform FSE and NJEMS tasks. Ability to develop and evaluate sampling plans and coordination of contract engagements for sampling events needed to evaluate human health exposure pathways.  Knowledge of CSRR rules, regulations, policies & guidance.  Experience with procurement operations of state contractors engaged to conduct sampling at contaminated sites.  Working knowledge of FSE and NJEMS.

Position 13 & 14

Review of remedial phase reports related to Educational Facilities and Child Care Centers, Review of remedial action reports for Unregulated Heating Oil Tank (UHOT) cases, Field audits of UHOT contractors, Oversight of permits by rule (PBR) related to UHOT cases, Preparation of on-scene coordinator permits (OSC) and oversight of such, Inspection of Educational Facilities and Child Care Centers, Inspection of deed notices, with or without Remedial Action Permits

EDUCATION:
Graduation from an accredited college or university with a Bachelor's degree in one of the Physical Sciences, Environmental Sciences/Studies, Chemical Sciences, or Biological Sciences; or in Environmental Planning, Environmental Policy, or Physical Geography; or in Civil Engineering, Sanitary Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Agricultural Engineering, Mining Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or Bio-resource Engineering.

NOTE: A valid Professional Engineer’s license issued by the New Jersey State Board of Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors may be substituted for the Bachelor’s degree in Engineering.

EXPERIENCE:
Two (2) years of experience in environmental control work including field investigations, inspection, and preparing reports on the environment or the preparation or review of Environmental Impact Statements.

NOTE: A Master's degree in one of the fields specified above may be substituted for one (1) year of the above experience.

jobs.title: Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) Manager
jobs.description:
Wish your job made a difference?

Our mission is protecting the world's water. We work every day to support the sustainability of our most precious resource, so our people know what they're doing matters.

Most importantly, you'll work with supportive teammates who have a strong work ethic and are committed to doing the right thing.

Join our team and do work that matters. Visit www.orenco.com/jobs to learn more or check out the official job description (below).

Company Description

Orenco Systems, Inc. (subsidiary of Infiltrator Water Technologies) is a manufacturer of innovative onsite and decentralized wastewater collection and treatment technologies. Solutions include community collection systems, advanced secondary treatment systems, watertight fiberglass tanks, and in-tank pumping and filtration systems. Orenco also manufactures high-quality standard, custom, and OEM controls, along with state-of-the-art fiberglass buildings, tanks, and enclosures.

Infiltrator Water Technologies is a market leader within the onsite wastewater treatment industry, Infiltrator manufactures a variety of revolutionary products and innovative, environmentally friendly alternatives to traditional stone and pipe leachfield and concrete septic wastewater system components. We sell our products through wholesale distribution across the United States and Canada for use on properties with onsite wastewater treatment systems.

Position Overview

Located in Sutherlin, OR, or Roseburg, OR

The EHS Manager oversees Environmental, Health, and Safety programs to ensure compliance and enhance operational resilience. Reporting to the Sr. EHS Manager, this role collaborates with cross-functional leaders to foster a proactive safety culture, maintain environmental regulatory compliance, and promote employee health initiatives. Key responsibilities include executing compliance tasks, leading field engagement, and providing support across EHS&S areas. The EHS Manager also provides strategic leadership and operational oversight, serving as an advisor to leadership and a partner to operations in driving safety, compliance, and environmental stewardship.

Core Responsibilities

Champion a positive safety culture and reinforce safe work practices across both locations.
Lead site health and safety processes, including behavior-based safety, risk assessments (TRA), mitigation strategies, ergonomics assessments, and Life Saving Principles reinforcement.
Model and maintain organizational safety, cultural, and professional standards.
Develop, implement, and lead safety, compliance, and preventative care programs, policies, and training.
Conduct audits, inspections, and compliance assessments; identify gaps and drive corrective and preventive actions.
Measure and evaluate the effectiveness of hazard management systems and recommend enhancements that drive risk reduction.
Lead incident investigations and root cause analysis (PDCA, Fishbone, 5-Why), ensuring corrective and preventive actions are implemented and verified.
Provide EHS performance reporting and data analysis to leadership.
Audit SOPs/MOPs and verify hazard analyses are completed for all manufacturing equipment.
Oversee core EHS programs including LOTO, Hazard Communication, EAP, Hearing Conservation, Hot Work, Respiratory Protection, and Bloodborne Pathogens.
Manage safety data systems, analytics, and OSHA recordkeeping to identify trends and drive continuous improvement.
Serve as the primary contact for all incidents, injuries, notifications, and case management.
Conduct required audits and support emergency response readiness, Safety Committee coordination, and shop floor-level EHS engagement.
Lead and support environmental compliance programs for Oregon state regulations and federal mandates, including but not limited to:
Title V Air Permitting
Tier II Reporting / EPCRA
Hazardous Waste (LQG) Compliance - RCRA
Stormwater Compliance & SWPPP
SPCC, Air Emissions, Waste Management, and Sustainability Programs
Conduct environmental inspections, sampling, testing, reporting, and documentation aligned with DEQ and EPA expectations.
Manage hazardous waste streams, universal waste, waste profiling, storage, characterization, and manifest requirements.
Maintain presence across both manufacturing sites and support off-shift needs when required.
Support sustainability initiatives, waste minimization efforts, and tracking of key environmental KPIs.
Drive near-miss reporting, learning, and closure of corrective actions.
Facilitate and monitor site security operations, including surveillance systems, access control processes, and coordinating with facilities, leadership, and third-party providers to ensure a secure, compliant, and disruption-free work environment.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety & Health, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, or related discipline.

QUALIFICATIONS (must Have)

Minimum 3 years of professional EHS experience in an industrial or manufacturing environment.
Demonstrated ability to create and deliver safety training programs.
Strong initiative with the ability to influence, coach, and facilitate change across diverse teams.
Capable of working independently with limited direction while maintaining strong cross-functional partnerships.
Excellent organizational habits with consistent follow-through.
Valid U.S. Driver's License.
Ability to travel domestically up to 10%.

QUALIFICATIONS (beneficial)

Strong interpersonal communication, project management capability, and structured problem-solving skills.
Effective presentation skills to support training delivery at all organizational levels.
Proficiency in interpreting and applying OSHA, EPA, DEQ, and other regulatory standards.
Skilled in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Teams) and EHS management systems.

Cell Phone

Computer

General Office Equipment

Vehicle

Office environment and indoor and outdoor manufacturing production environments.

Regular job duties include seeing, speaking, hearing, reading, writing, keyboarding, periods of sitting including time viewing a computer screen. Time on manufacturing floor includes prolonged periods of standing and walking on concrete floors, kneeling, climbing stairs and ladders, reaching, pushing, pulling, grasping, holding, measuring, cutting, stacking, bending, twisting, stooping, squatting, repetitive foot and hand movement with good manual dexterity. UMIAQ Environmental is seeking a knowledgeable and detail-oriented RCRA Waste Compliance Specialist/Inspector to join our team. This role will ensure facilities comply with the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) regulations related to nonhazardous and hazardous waste management. Primary duties include conducting inspections, audits, and evaluations to ensure compliance with federal, state, and local hazardous waste regulations. Additionally, the role involves providing guidance and technical support to regulated entities to promote best practices in hazardous waste handling, storage, and disposal.

Responsibilities

Essential functions will include:

Comprehensive RCRA environmental consulting includes planning, data assessment, reporting, overseeing field personnel, travel, fieldwork, and/or sample collection.
Review, evaluate, and interpret environmental data and prepare summary reports.
Interact and communicate with clients, vendors, and staff at all levels in a professional manner.

Receive, review, prepare, and sign shipping documents.
Convert shipping documents.
Audit/ perform checks on employees and procedures.
Writing work instructions and SOPs

Experience sampling soil, groundwater, and other media at contaminated sites.
Experience in hazardous waste and hazardous materials management.

Excellent writing, organizational, and communication skills required to interact with clients and staff at all levels effectively.
Must be personable, flexible, and professional.
Must be able to work independently with minimal supervision.
Must have and maintain a valid driver license and insurable driving record.
Experience with planning, logistics, and fieldwork in remote locations.

Frequent walking, standing, twisting, and turning of the upper body, arms, and legs.

Senior Environmental Planner | Hybrid

VHB is actively seeking a Senior Environmental Planner to enrich our New England team. This role will be leading and supporting the preparation of federal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) and Massachusetts Environmental Policy Act (MEPA) documentation, as well as permitting applications, for a diverse set of clients.

At VHB, we specialize in delivering comprehensive environmental services to an array of clients, including municipalities, transportation agencies, airports, energy firms, private developers, and more. Our offerings encompass intricate technical analyses, both short and long-term planning solutions, as well as strategic environmental permitting strategies. Our objective is to not only meet regulatory standards but also to advance sustainability objectives and comprehend the impacts of our built environment.

We are in search of an adept professional with a proven track record in devising sustainable solutions for large-scale infrastructure endeavors. This role extends beyond project oversight, encompassing the leadership of diverse teams engaged in environmental planning and permitting across a broad spectrum of clients and projects.

Within VHB’s expansive environmental realm, our team delivers a spectrum of services ranging from environmental permitting to sustainability and resilience planning. This includes areas such as energy policy, climate action planning, net-zero emissions strategies, climate vulnerability assessments, urban and regional planning, solid waste management, air quality and noise studies, natural resource stewardship, water conservation, historic resource management, and community engagement initiatives. We seek candidates who not only possess a deep understanding of these services but also exhibit a keen interest in contributing to our full range of environmental endeavors.

Coordinate with clients and manage environmental projects including technical subconsultants.
Drive business development activities including preparing scopes of work, fee estimates, and schedules.
Review environmental studies and work prepared by others.
Prepare environmental documentation and presentations.
Manage environmental scopes and budgets amongst a diverse range of technical resource groups.
Oversee the facilitation of stakeholder meetings, public workshops, and public hearings.
A passion for coaching and/or mentoring skills is required.
Ability to travel occasionally.

Strong understanding of NEPA and MEPA (or similar state processes) as it relates to Transportation/DOT or similar projects.

jobs.description:
Description

JOB SUMMARY

The Senior Environmental Engineer serves as a strategic technical leader responsible for the oversight and execution of environmental compliance, permitting, and sustainability programs. This role involves managing complex regulatory requirements at the local, state, and federal levels, specifically as they relate to mining, aggregates, asphalt, and building materials production.

You will act as a primary liaison between operations and regulatory agencies, ensuring that all sites within your district operate within the law while minimizing their environmental footprint. The position requires a high degree of independence, a proactive 'self-starter' mindset, and the ability to provide technical mentorship to junior staff and production teams.

Key Duties And Responsibilities

Administer the full lifecycle of environmental permits (Air Quality, NPDES, Water Rights, US Army Corps, Wetlands, and Endangered Species).
Lead the development and implementation of critical environmental plans, including SWPPP (Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans) and SPCC (Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure).
Manage the timely submission of all regulatory reports, including Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs) and annual emissions inventories.
Build and maintain professional relationships with local, state, and federal regulators; represent the company at public hearings and permit actions.
Conduct regular site inspections and recordkeeping reviews to identify potential risks.
Provide hands-on guidance to Plant Managers and Production staff on best practices for water discharge, oil storage, and waste management.

jobs.description:
Location: Toronto-661 University

Department: Data Science and Analytics

This posting is to fill a current vacancy.

The Role

To provide geospatial analytics expertise that transforms data into actionable intelligence, supporting surveillance, population health assessment, public health planning, research, and evidence-informed decision-making across Public Health Ontario and the broader public health system.

To advance PHO's capacity in geospatial analysis, spatial data management, and geographic information systems by developing innovative analytical approaches, visualizations, and decision-support products that address public health priorities, population health issues, and emerging health threats.

Key Responsibilities-

Develops, maintains, and enhances integrated geospatial data assets from internal and external sources, applying data quality, metadata, and governance practices to support public health analytics and decision-making.
Develops geospatial analyses, visualizations, and spatial intelligence products that support surveillance, epidemiology, population and health system assessment, research, planning, and data science initiatives.
Collaborates with multidisciplinary teams to apply spatial modelling, hotspot detection, population characterization, accessibility analysis, and risk factor analysis to public health priorities, population health issues, health equity considerations, and emerging health threats.
Promotes the adoption of innovative geospatial methods and technologies that advance PHO strategic priorities and strengthen evidence-informed public health practice.
Acquires, integrates, analyzes, interprets, and assesses the quality of administrative, demographic, socioeconomic, environmental, remote sensing, health, and other relevant data.
Identifies and manages spatial reference data, including geographic boundaries, service locations, points of interest, and environmental features of public health relevance.
Serves as a subject matter expert in geospatial analytics, advising PHO and collaborating with external organizations on data standards, data-sharing practices, analytical methods, and geospatial capabilities.
Evaluates emerging geospatial trends, technologies, standards, and practices for appropriate application within PHO.
Communicates geospatial findings through maps, dashboards, interactive applications, reports, presentations, and scientific forums, and represents PHO in relevant collaborations.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Knowledge And Skills-

Proficiency in cartographic design, geospatial visualization, geostatistics, spatial modelling, and spatial data analysis, including communicating complex information through maps, dashboards, interactive applications, and other decision-support products.
Knowledge of geospatial data platforms, cloud and web mapping technologies, spatial databases, data integration tools, and practices used to develop, share, and sustain geospatial products.
Knowledge of geospatial theories, methods, and geographic concepts and their application to public health analysis and decision-making.
Knowledge of geospatial data management and governance, including raster and vector data models, spatial databases, metadata standards, data quality, privacy, security, and information management principles.
Knowledge of public health, epidemiology, population health, health equity, environmental determinants of health, and health system concepts relevant to geospatial analysis.
Knowledge of applicable privacy, security, ethical, and data stewardship requirements for collecting, using, linking, visualizing, and sharing health and geospatial data, including Indigenous data governance considerations.
Demonstrated commitment to continuous learning in geospatial analytics, data science, public health intelligence, and related technologies.

Education And Experience-

Bachelor’s degree in geography, geomatics, geographic information systems (GIS), spatial data science, epidemiology, public health, environmental science, data science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
A minimum of five years’ work experience with GIS and geospatial analysis.
Advanced knowledge of enterprise and open-source GIS and geospatial analytics platforms, with experience in spatial analysis, web mapping, scripting, automation, application development, APIs, and relevant programming and query languages.
Experience with PHO-supported technologies such as ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Online, Python, SQL, and R is an asset.

Attributes and Competencies-

Oral, written, visual, and interpersonal communication skills to translate complex geospatial findings into clear, accessible insights for technical, non-technical, and executive audiences.
Consultation, facilitation, and presentation skills to gather requirements, explain analytical methods and limitations, and communicate findings and recommendations through reports, maps, dashboards, interactive products, and presentations.
Develops collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders to understand needs and deliver responsive geospatial analytics and decision-support services for public health priorities, population health issues, and emerging health threats.
Responds to requests for geospatial analysis, visualization, data, metadata, and related documentation, clarifying the intended use and appropriate analytical approach.
Defines client needs, requirements, deliverables, success criteria, and application requirements for geospatial initiatives.
Coordinates assigned geospatial initiatives through planning, delivery, and evaluation to support timely, fit-for purpose results and stakeholder satisfaction.
Advises on the application of geospatial analytics to surveillance, population health and health system assessment, health equity, program and service planning, resource allocation, and response to emerging health threats.
Assesses stakeholder information and analytical requirements and selects appropriate methods for analyzing, visualizing, and communicating spatial information to support public health planning, surveillance, resource allocation, service access, and response activities.
Evaluates available data sources, analytical methods, assumptions, and limitations to determine their suitability for public health use.
Determines how spatial and non-spatial data can be linked, analyzed, and presented to generate actionable insights on public health priorities, population health issues, and emerging health threats.
Delivers accurate, timely, and fit-for-purpose geospatial analyses and decision-support products that inform surveillance, population and health system assessment, health equity, climate and environmental health, service planning, resource allocation, and response to emerging health threats.
Generates spatial insights on patterns, trends, access, inequities, populations, and environmental and social determinants to support evidence-informed public health planning and action.
Provides geospatial subject matter expertise and project leadership within cross-functional teams and initiatives.
Builds team capability through coaching, mentoring, and knowledge exchange on geospatial methods, tools, and interpretation.

jobs.description:
About The Role

Balfour Beatty are looking for a Senior Geo-Environmental Engineer to join thier Power T&D Division in Derby.

Role Purpose

Providing technical support, advice, strategy and direction to the geotechnical and geo-environmental team leader and wider team.

You will deliver integrated site assessments that inform planning, design and remediation strategies.

You will work with the project team, designers and subcontractors through the design phase to deliver safe and suitable scope of works in line with the project objectives and then deliver these to a high standard.

The role includes leading Phase 1 and 2 site and ground investigations and ensuring the production of high-quality technical reporting deliverables, and the development of practical, cost-effective remediation approaches to all projects secured by Balfour Beatty Power Transmission and Distribution (BB PT&D).

Balfour Beatty welcomes applications from both full-time and part-time candidates, including those interested in job-sharing arrangements. Additionally, the company offers a flexible working policy to support a healthy work-life balance.

What you'll be doing

Key Accountabilities

To undertake Phase 1 and Phase 2 geotechnical and geo-environmental assessment as required for OHL, Cabling and Substation projects, from the initial feasibility assessment, through desk study phase and design development to detailed design & delivery / construction phase and scheme closure ensuring completion in accordance with programme, cost and quality requirements.
Ensure the timely and quality delivery of designs to meet budget, programme and pre-determined objectives. Preparation of reports, calculations and drawings to a high technical level which are compliant with the required Client and national technical standards (BS/Eurocodes/ENA).
Checking of other work packages

Key Responsibilities

Design appropriate investigation works to allow for a detailed land contamination assessment and plan for remedial works to suitably remediate contaminated land where proven to exist. Including:

Lead start-to-end delivery of Phase 1 Feasibility and Desktop Studies, Phase 2 Ground Investigations, and follow on remediation strategy and verification works.
Manage multi-disciplinary ground investigations, integrating geotechnical and geo-environmental in-situ and laboratory based test results and other data provision, management and assessments.
Produce GI specifications and schedules and where required contract documents, manage GI contractors and support with exploratory hole termination advice and decisions, installation design and details, sampling, backfill and scheduling of geotechnical and chemical laboratory testing schedules.
Produce high quality and comprehensive geotechnical and geo-environmental factual and interpretative reports, undertake contamination risk assessments with evaluation of ground conditions and design parameters where necessary.
Provide technical input into foundation and infrastructure assessment and design, ground improvement strategies, and remediation schemes
Build and maintain close and strong working relationships with clients, consultants and regulatory bodies.
Schedule chemical testing , analyse and present findings of contamination assessments clearly and support clients to satisfying planning and other regulatory conditions and achieve environmental compliance
Provide on site assessment of geological conditions resulting in design decisions for applicable engineering solutions.
Undertake assessment on the condition and nature of materials and advise on their acceptability for re-use.
Prepare accurate costings, monitor budgets, and drive efficient and timely project delivery in the team.
Appoint, liaise with and manage subcontractors to support delivery of their reports and deliverables.
Devise training plans to upskill and support junior engineers in the team and staff across to be competent in areas of environmental and land contamination assessment including line management responsibilities?
Working closely with Project Teams to determine and maintain common objectives and to ensure work undertaken is appropriate and in accordance with project priorities.
Embed “Safety by Design” principles in all activities, including managing safety through appropriate life cycle designs that minimise risks to personnel and property, by ensuring that Health & Safety Regulations and Balfour Beatty procedures and requirements are followed in the design substation, cabling and OHL projects.

Who we're looking for

Skills Required

Degree level education or equivalent with formal training in geology, civil engineering and/or geotechnical engineering.
Professional membership of either the ICE or Geol Soc & working towards Chartered Engineer status with the aim of achieving this within the next year to two years maximum period of time.
Experience of coordinating with government agencies and local authorities such as SEPA, EA etc
Strong, proven post-graduate track record and level of experience in the civil engineering industry
Proven experience in both geotechnical and geo-environmental project delivery.
Strong technical report writing skills, including Phase 1 & 2 desk study and GIR assessments
Working knowledge of remediation processes and environmental modelling
Practical understanding of ground conditions and foundation types and behaviour
Experience of the supervision and/or monitoring of sub-contractors
Proven experience of the design of large scale civil engineering works
Strong, proven experience of the management of design of civil or geotechnical engineering works
IT Literate (Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel)
Extensive experience of geotechnical design software including slope and retention design packages

Why work for us

Day in, day out, our teams deliver some of the UK’s most ambitious, exciting and meaningful projects; developing, building and maintaining the vital infrastructure that supports national economies and strengthens communities.

Benefits

As if contributing to and supporting work that makes life better for millions wasn’t rewarding enough, we offer a full range of benefits too. You’ll have the freedom to shape the package that’s right for you and your life. Here are some of our key benefits:

Smart working, giving you more flexibility such as staggered start and finish times, with up to 40% remote working, where roles allow.
25 days paid annual leave (pro rata)
Family friendly policies which include 28 weeks full pay for maternity/adoption leave and four weeks full pay for paternity/partners leave
Pension, share incentive plan, volunteering leave, recognition schemes and much more…

About Us

Balfour Beatty’s Power Transmission & Distribution teams work with regional, national and international electricity network owners and operators to provide technical engineering solutions across the full spectrum of the electricity grid, including overhead lines, cabling, substations and distribution networks.

From scoping and feasibility, to design, construction and on-going maintenance, our in-house experts, flexible resources and industry-leading innovations support customers in the development of some of the UK’s most ambitious power transmission and distribution projects.

Diversity and inclusion

Through our Value Everyone Diversity and Inclusion Strategy and Action Plan, we are growing our diverse workforce and developing our inclusive culture where everyone is able to thrive and reach their full potential, regardless of their identity or background.
