jobs.title: Associate Principal, Portfolio Project Management (Environmental & Social Consulting)
jobs.description:
Bring Clarity to Complexity

At Two Worlds Consulting, we help clients navigate complex social, environmental, and regulatory challenges by bringing together Indigenous Knowledge and Western science. Working collaboratively with First Nations, Métis, Inuit, industry, and the public sector, we support informed decision-making through practical, culturally grounded, and technically sound solutions.

We are seeking an Associate Principal, Portfolio Project Management
to provide project management leadership across our portfolio of small to medium-sized projects. The role balances direct management of individual projects with oversight of portfolio performance, resourcing, risk, and delivery outcomes.

The successful candidate will lead multidisciplinary teams in the delivery of human environment, archaeology, environmental, and related consulting services for a wide range of clients. Working closely with other Project Managers, Project Coordinators, Principals, and Associate Principals, they will monitor portfolio performance, identify and address emerging risks and resourcing needs, and help ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to a high standard of quality.

This position is well-suited to individuals who are confident Project Managers, thrive in collaborative and relationship-focused environments, and can balance hands-on project delivery with responsibility for the health and performance of a portfolio of work.

Compensation

$120,000 - $140,000 per year. Compensation is based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated expertise, with flexibility for exceptional candidates.

Location

Remote within Canada (home-based, with occasional travel). Hybrid or office-based options available for candidates located in Victoria or Vancouver, BC.

What You'll Do

Portfolio Management
Provide leadership and oversight for our portfolio of small to medium sized consulting projects, supporting successful delivery, effective resource utilization, financial performance, and a consistently high standard of client service.
Monitor portfolio performance and business-level portfolio health, including scope, schedule, budget, quality, capacity, utilization, backlog, revenue, margin, delivery risk, client relationship health, and alignment between current work, upcoming opportunities, and available resources.
Collaborate with Project Managers, Principals, and Directors to support prioritization, resource planning, workload management, and consistent delivery practices across the portfolio.
Develop and promote efficient project management practices, processes, reporting, and delivery standards across portfolio projects.
Support and mentor Project Managers, Principals, and other team members by sharing project management expertise and contributing to professional growth and development.
Foster a positive, collaborative team environment that supports engagement, accountability, learning, and recognition.

Project Management
Build and maintain positive client relationships focused on delivering high-quality services and fostering long-term partnerships across TWC service areas.
Develop proposals and support business development activities, including scope development, budgeting, resourcing, project planning, execution, and communication of project status and outcomes.
Manage project scope, budget, schedule, and quality.
Work with the Principals in Charge to lead project teams and provide direction and oversight of project activities to support successful project outcomes.
Maintain a strong understanding of TWC's service areas, project delivery approaches, relevant legislation, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
Ensure projects are delivered in alignment with client requirements, contractual obligations, corporate values, health and safety policies, and applicable regulatory standards.
Support timely invoicing, financial tracking, and client payment processes across assigned projects

What We're Looking For

We welcome applications from candidates who may not meet every qualification but bring relevant consulting experience, lived or professional insight, and a strong alignment with our work.

Required Qualifications
10+ years of progressively responsible project management experience in a consulting, professional services, or related environment, including responsibility for multiple concurrent projects or a portfolio of work with accountability for scope, budgets, schedules, resources, client relationships, and delivery outcomes.
Project management training, certification, or designation (e.g., PMP).
Experience delivering consulting services for Indigenous Nations, government, industry, or other clients in areas such as engagement, human environment, planning, stewardship, advisory services, environmental management, or related fields. 
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and working collaboratively with technical specialists, Project Managers, clients, and other stakeholders to deliver successful project outcomes.
Strong leadership, relationship-building, and communication skills, including experience mentoring team members, resolving challenges, and delivering exceptional client service.
Strong project and business management skills, including proposal development, budgeting, forecasting, resource planning, financial management, and risk mitigation.
Strong understanding of reconciliation and the diverse rights, priorities, perspectives, and governance structures of Indigenous Peoples in Canada.
Degree or diploma from an accredited post-secondary institution in a relevant discipline, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and project management tools.
Alignment with TWC's values and principles, with the ability to thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced, and dynamic consulting environment.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience managing significant annual revenue portfolios and supporting resource planning and delivery oversight.
Experience working with geographically distributed or remote teams.
Indigenous lived experience that contributes to team-based, multi-lens project delivery and helps inform how Indigenous perspectives are collectively understood, represented, and integrated into consulting work.

About Two Worlds Consulting

Founded in 2016, Two Worlds Consulting supports clients across Canada through a multi-lens approach that respectfully brings together Indigenous Knowledge and Western scientific methods. Guided by respect, reciprocity, trust, and integrity, we are known for building strong relationships, delivering technical excellence, and helping clients and communities navigate complex decisions with confidence.

Our team works across sectors including mining, energy, infrastructure, transportation, government, and Indigenous community initiatives.

Learn more at twoworldsconsulting.com.

Key Areas

Environmental Consulting, Social Consulting, Project Management, Portfolio Management, Community and Culture, Human Environment, Engagement, Rights and Interests Assessment, Indigenous Knowledge, Socio-economic Services, Impact Assessment, Environmental Assessment, Policy, Planning, and Regulatory Processes.

Posting Close Date

Please submit your application by 5:00pm PST September 16, 2026.

jobs.description:
Design a career and build your future... Because it matters!

GIS Specialist

McMillen Inc. is looking for a GIS Specialist
to join our Geospatial Group
. In this role, you’ll support scientific and engineering initiatives through cartography, geospatial analysis, data visualization, and spatial data management. Initially, your primary focus will be developing maps and managing geospatial data for permitting and engineering projects. As you grow in the role, you’ll have opportunities to apply your geospatial expertise to a variety of science and engineering studies based on your experience and interests. You’ll be expected to independently manage GIS efforts across multiple projects while contributing advanced geospatial solutions to our multidisciplinary team.

Who we are:
McMillen, Inc. designs and builds solutions that shape the future of water resources. As an employee-owned firm, we take pride in every project because we know our work truly matters. Our people thrive on solving complex challenges, pushing boundaries, and refining their craft. We don’t look for the complacent or the comfortable. We seek problem solvers, innovators, and experts who are always striving to be better. We support continuous learning, cutting-edge technology, and a balanced work-life environment so our employees can build careers they’re proud of.

We are focused in the dams, energy, fisheries, natural resources, and infrastructure markets. Our people integrate engineering, environmental, and construction expertise to deliver practical, results-driven outcomes. From concept to completion, projects are guided through feasibility studies, permitting, design, construction, and commissioning, ensuring technical precision and real-world functionality.

Responsibilities:

Develop professional-quality maps and cartographic products using ArcGIS Pro
Manage and organize geospatial datasets for engineering and permitting projects
Perform geospatial analysis to support environmental, engineering, and scientific initiatives
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver innovative GIS solutions
Maintain GIS databases (including metadata) and ensure data quality and accuracy
Develop surveys for field data collection using Field Maps Designer and Survey123
Opportunities to develop web applications (e.g., ArGIS Experience Builder, ArGIS Dashboards, Leaflet, and others) as time and interest allows

Qualifications:

0-5 years of experience applying GIS and spatial analysis in support of engineering, hydrology, or environmental science projects
Bachelor’s degree in in an environmental science field with applied geospatial and GIS component or credential.
Experience with ArcGIS Pro
Experience with ArcGIS Online and ESRI web-based applications
Intermediate experience creating professional cartographic products
Understanding of geospatial analysis concepts, including spatial statistics and the Spatial Analyst toolkit (or equivalent open-source tools)
Knowledge of spatial projections and datums
Experience working with geospatial data, including: ESRI Geodatabases, KML, GeoPackage, JSON, Elevation data (DEM, point clouds, TIN), and Satellite imagery (Sentinel, Landsat), Derived Products (Land Cover/Classification)
Strong curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn new software and technologies
Ability to support multiple technical disciplines and projects simultaneously
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across disciplines and convey technical concepts to varied audiences.
Strong organization and data management skills.
Knowledge of QGIS and Google Earth Engine preferred
Knowledge of programming languages such as python, R, SQL, and Arcade (ESRI) preferred
Familiarity with geospatial libraries such as GDAL and GRASS GIS preferred.

ERG is a research and consulting firm that provides a wide range of support to federal, state, and commercial clients. ERG offers multidisciplinary teams with nationally recognized skills in engineering, science, economics, public health, informational technology, and communications. We hire people with the best minds and then provide them with a vibrant and flexible environment in which to develop their careers. The qualified individual must be highly motivated with the skills to prioritize, perform, and communicate effectively in a fast-paced environment. 

ERG’s Environmental and Occupational Health Group has an immediate opening for an early career professional to join our multi-disciplinary team. This individual will support a range of environmental and sustainability-related projects, including a clean energy grant program. The qualified individual must be highly motivated with the skills to prioritize, perform, and communicate effectively in a fast-paced environment. Responsibilities include managing large datasets, working with applicants to meet grant program requirements, using grant management software and related database applications to support client needs, and interfacing directly with clients.

Ideal candidates will have direct experience developing and supporting data visualization tools; conducting independent research and data analysis; and providing client services.

Review clean energy grant applications for eligibility and completeness

Process payment requests and interface with applicants throughout the grant process

Identify and categorize potential application errors and communicate them to applicants and clients

Help develop and maintain a public-facing government data dashboard

Analyze, collect, and organize data to support greenhouse gas, energy, and water reduction projects, benchmarking, and reporting

Research and develop briefing materials on sustainability topics, including decarbonization and building and fleet electrification

Provide additional data analysis and technical communications support on environmental, sustainability, and public health topics

Qualifications and Skills:

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science or a related field

Minimum of one year of experience working with environmental or sustainability-related data

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other data management tools preferred

Experience with data visualization software, such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, or Qlik Sense

Familiarity with energy efficiency improvements, water conservation measures, and greenhouse gas emissions inventories

Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, including experience drafting technical reports and presenting findings

Experience working with and managing large, complex datasets

Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary team

Strong interpersonal skills with a customer service focus

Ability to take initiative, stay organized, and manage multiple tasks

ERG offers competitive salaries and excellent benefits, including health and dental insurance, life insurance, long-term disability, educational benefits, FSAs, a generous 401k plan, profit sharing, an EAP, 11-20 paid vacation days per year, 10 paid holidays per year, 56 hours or more of sick leave (based on the state you work in) per year (pro-rated for part-time) and more. jobs.description:
Take Your Environmental Career to the Next Level

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step into Your New Role

We are seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist / Ecologist
to join our EP&P team in our Sewickley, PA office.

Job Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will lead field teams in wetland delineations, prepare technical reports, prepare permitting applications to federal, state, and local entities, manage the environmental task in project schedules, and coordinate with internal and external groups to complete project tasks and goals. This is a client facing role, the candidate will be required to convey project related information to a variety of clients. The work will involve primarily technical writing for permitting, environmental task management, and leading field efforts including wetland delineations, site assessments, environmental inspections, endangered species surveys, habitat assessments, and other studies.

Position Requirements:

7-15 years of consulting experience.
Experience conducting wetland delineations in accordance with the USACE 1987 Wetland Delineation Manual and supporting Regional Supplements.
Excellent technical writing and verbal communication skills.
Comprehensive understanding and experience preparing of Section 404, 10, and 401WQC.
Knowledge of environmental laws and regulations, specifically pertaining to wetlands and listed wildlife species.
Ability to work flexible work schedules and availability to meet priority deadlines outside of normal working hours.
A valid driver's license.

Education & Certifications:

BS in an Environmental, Biological or Ecological Science, or Environmental Policy; Masters in a relevant field of study is a plus.
40-hour USACE wetland training.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

Plant and wildlife identification skills and survey and permitting protocols.
Excellent planning and organizational skills with strong problem-solving abilities and analytical skills.
Experience operating GPS units under ArcGIS or Terrasync programs.
Experience in ArcGIS or AutoCAD.
Ability to conduct work year-round in adverse climate and field conditions.
Ability to prioritize effort and effectively be engaged on multiple projects at one time.
Experience developing and completing Threatened and endangered species surveys, and coordination with the USFWS

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

Move Forward with Kleinfelder:
 Kleinfelder and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, has been connecting great people to the best work since 1961. We are engineers, scientists, and construction professionals providing solutions that improve our clients’ transportation, water, energy, and other private infrastructure. As a responsive, cross-disciplinary team of bright, curious, and innovative problem-solvers, we are dedicated to doing the right thing, every day, on every project from over 110 offices in the US, Canada, and Australia. Connecting great people to the best work is our purpose – together, we deliver. 

Progress with an Employer that Values You

Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, is an inclusive organization free from discrimination. We are a stronger organization when we are a diverse workforce and believe that through diversity, equity, and inclusion comes creativity, innovation, and unity. We are proud to offer the following: 

Benefits:
Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, offers an excellent compensation and benefits package, including: medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) plan, and paid holidays.

Career Development:
We are committed to investing in the professional development of our staff, offering each employee every opportunity to grow, develop, and take control of their career paths. We support these efforts through reimbursements for continuing education as well as many of the expenses associated with trainings and certifications, and opportunities for career development through our internal Mentoring Program.

Equal Opportunity:
Kleinfelder, and its’ subsidiaries and affiliates, is an Equal Opportunity Employer – Minorities/Women/Disabled/Veterans. (Compliant with the new VEVRAA and Section 503 rules)

jobs.title: Environmental Advisor
jobs.description:
Equans Data Centers are seeking to appoint an Environmental Advisor to support the growth in our data center sector.

Our commitment is to provide cutting edge solutions for our clients Data Center facilities. We are recruiting an Environmental Advisor to work with our project team to provide support our aim towards decarbonisation.

Based on the construction sites, the successful candidate will be the main point of contact for all Environmental management within the Data Center sites. This role will include regular travel to sites across the South.

What you will deliver?

Organise and arrange all site level environmental monitoring, measurement and reporting for all regulatory, compliance and business purposes
Assist with the delivery of central carbon reduction targets for projects
Implement waste reduction plans involving circular economy and waste diversion resulting in waste prevention
Embed Sustainable practices on site delivering training and toolbox talks and support the identification and implementation of preventative measures
Assist the project teams to achieve BREEAM/LEED rating and certification when required
Provide guidance and ensure that Project Teams are effectively managing all relevant environmental aspects to reduce risk on site
Act as a site level advisor on business related local and national environmental regulatory requirements
Monitor and report on our environmental performance and regularly undertake site level inspections
Assist in the preparation and review of project environmental documents
Assist the Project Teams in the management and investigation of environmental incidents
Complete regular internal environmental reports highlighting site performance against current KPI’s
Collaborate with the central Environmental & Sustainability team in driving the environmental agenda by improving performance across the data center business area and companywide though written communications.
Upskill and support teams, acting as a facilitator when delivering site based environmental training
When required, act as an advisor to clients for any environmentally related issues or activities
Review and discuss internal environmental reports highlighting site performance against current KPI’s
Ensure that sites have all correct permits and licences for conducting any activities that have an environmental impact.

What we can offer you?

On offer is a competitive salary and benefits package, which includes;

25 days annual leave (+ public holidays)
Life Cover equivalent to 4 times annual salary
Company Stakeholder Pension Scheme
Private Medical Insurance
2 corporate social responsibility days per year
Broad range of learning opportunities, such as professional qualifications, collective/individual training, and personalised support programmes
Attractive Employee Referral Rewards Scheme
Access to our growing employee networks including AccessAbility (representing those with physical and mental disabilities), Encompass (representing the LGBTQ+ community), RISE (representing people from ethnic backgrounds), Veterans & Reservists, WOMEN TOGETHER (representing women in Equans), Working Parents, and Young Professionals.
24/7 Employee Assistance Program and access to mental wellbeing app

Who are we looking for?

Previous experience as an Environmental Advisor or similar role
Knowledge of the application of ISO14001
Technical familiarity with environmental processes and assessments e.g. BREEAM/LEED knowledge and Advisory Professional certification
Strong background in assessment of environmental hazards and understanding of the mechanisms of how to mitigate
Ability to work independently and be self-motivated
High level of personal drive and commitment with the desire to progress
Effective communication skills with the ability to build relationships across all levels of the organisation.
Competent report writing skills
Professional and pragmatic team player who can build and sustain effective working relationships
Degree qualification in a relevant discipline e.g. Environmental Management /Sciences or Sustainability, with professional body membership (IEMA, IES or CIEEM) preferred
Practitioner Membership with IEMA or similar professional membership, or working towards would be advantageous
Experience of the Construction or a related industry would be desirable
Willingness and ability to travel nationally across projects

Who are we?

Equans Data Centers is a strategic data centre partner. We deliver the whole data centre, providing full general contracting for hyperscaler and colocation data centre projects across Europe, through a single point of contact.

Leveraging Bouygues Energies & Services and Equans Group' experiences, we provide expertise in construction and engineering, global standardisation, precision localisation and total control of the supply chain. This enables us to deliver data centres with the best possible quality, speed to delivery and high repeatability and scalability – to realise client needs for cost transparency, low risk, continual availability, innovation and certainty of planning and outcomes.

With more than 1,200 highly skilled employees across 8 European countries, Equans Data Centres has delivered over 400,000m2 of data halls, exceeding 640MW of IT space for major data centres providers such as VIRTUS Data Centers, Digital Reality, Equinix, Vantage Data Centers, Stack Infrastructure, Data4 and many others.

What’s next?

If this role is of interest to you, please click below to register, apply, and track your progress! A member of our Resourcing Team will review your application and be in touch. 

As part our commitment to better reflect the markets within which we operate, we encourage applications from women, ethnically diverse individuals and people with disabilities, along with all candidates who identify with protected characteristic groups under the Equality Act 2010.

At Equans we’re committed to delivering a culture where everyone’s voice is heard and supported. We know the value a diverse workforce creates, delivering better results for our people, customers, and stakeholders. Diversity and inclusion is at the core of what we do, should you join Equans you’ll find a welcoming and open workplace where you’re supported and encouraged to be your true self at work.

You’ll also have access to our growing employee networks including AccessAbility (representing those with physical and mental disabilities), Encompass (representing the LGBTQ+ community), RISE (representing people from ethnic backgrounds), Veterans & Reservists, WOMEN Together (representing women in Equans), Working Parents, and Young Professionals.

For this role, you must have evidence of the right to work in the UK. Unfortunately, we are not able to offer a re-location package with this job role.  Certain roles may require applicants to undergo a Disclosure check, as noted in the role requirements. 

The EQUANS Resourcing Team supports this job advert. Agency involvement is not required. All related enquiries must come to the resourcing team not direct to EQUANS Managers.

Our Environmental group is looking for an Environmental Scientist
to join their team! As a graduate with this group, you will be engaged with projects that involve wetland delineations/assessments & permitting, endangered species surveys, water quality assessments, and ecological & environmental studies. These projects support ecological risk assessments, site characterization and remedial action projects on contaminated sites.

Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Ecological assessments to classify and map habitat cover types and plant communities
Surface water quality monitoring and sampling
Sediment sampling
Macroinverterate surveys / sampling
Fish, reptile and amphibian surveys
Managing and evaluating chemical and biological data
Evaluating and understanding environmental regulations
Preparing work plans, reports and other written communications

Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Biology, Ecology or related field of study
0-2 years of experience conducting wetland delineations and ecological field studies
Proficiency with managing and evaluating chemical and biological data using spreadsheets or database software
Familiarity with geographic information systems (GIS) applications software

jobs.description:
Job Description
: Geospatial Business Development Specialist - Southern California
Territory:
Irvine/Orange County, Inland Empire & San Diego

Build Your Career. Own Your Territory. Grow With Us.

AeroTech Mapping, Inc. is seeking a motivated, relationship-driven Geospatial Business Development Specialist to lead business development efforts throughout Los Angeles County and Southern California.

This is an opportunity for an ambitious sales professional who wants the freedom to manage their own territory, build lasting client relationships, and directly influence their income and career growth. We are not looking for someone who requires constant direction; we are looking for a self-starter who thrives in a flexible, remote work environment and takes ownership of their success.

You will represent one of the Southwest's leading aerial mapping, LiDAR, surveying, and geospatial firms while partnering with engineering companies, public agencies, utilities, developers, and infrastructure clients throughout Southern California.

What You'll Do

As a Geospatial Business Development Specialist, you will be responsible for growing and managing a sales territory while developing long-term relationships with clients and industry partners.

Key Responsibilities

·      Identify, pursue, and secure new business opportunities within assigned markets and territories
·      Build and maintain relationships with engineering firms, government agencies, utilities, developers, and other industry stakeholders
·      Promote AeroTech Mapping's aerial mapping, LiDAR, surveying, orthophotography, GIS, remote sensing, and geospatial solutions
·      Develop and execute strategic account plans to achieve sales and growth objectives
·      Attend industry conferences, trade shows, networking events, and client meetings
·      Conduct presentations and educational sessions highlighting AeroTech's capabilities and services
·      Collaborate with technical and proposal teams to develop winning strategies and client-focused solutions
·      Maintain accurate sales activities, opportunities, and client communications within Salesforce CRM
·      Monitor market trends, industry developments, and competitor activity
·      Manage and grow existing client relationships while continually developing new opportunities
·      Serve as a trusted advisor to clients throughout the project lifecycle

What Makes This Opportunity Different

·      Remote and flexible work environment
·      High degree of autonomy and trust
·      Established reputation with over 20 years in the geospatial industry
·      Strong technical support team allowing you to focus on relationship building and sales
·      Opportunity to grow your territory and income
·      Long-term career path with leadership potential
·      Collaborative culture that values initiative and accountability over micromanagement

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications
·      3+ years of business development, sales, account management, or client relationship experience
·      Proven ability to develop and maintain professional relationships
·      Strong communication, presentation, and networking skills
·      Self-starter with excellent time management and organizational skills
·      Ability to work independently while remaining connected to a remote team
·      Experience using CRM systems such as Salesforce or similar platforms
·      Willingness to travel throughout assigned territories as needed

Preferred Qualifications
·      Experience in the A/E/C, geospatial, surveying, engineering, construction, utility, transportation, or technology industries
·      Understanding of aerial mapping, LiDAR, GIS, surveying, remote sensing, or related technologies
·      Experience responding to proposals, RFQs, or public agency procurement processes
·      Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Geography, Engineering, GIS, Surveying, or a related field
·      Ability to travel throughout Southern California for client meetings, industry events, and conferences

The Ideal Candidate

You are:
·      Entrepreneurial and motivated by achieving goals
·      Comfortable working independently without constant supervision
·      Naturally curious and relationship-driven
·      Competitive, resilient, and energized by creating opportunities
·      Looking for a long-term career rather than a short-term job
·      Interested in becoming a recognized industry professional and trusted client advisor
·      Energetic and driven to expand AeroTech's presence throughout Southern California

Compensation & Benefits

·      Competitive base salary plus performance-based incentives
·      Medical, dental, and vision insurance
·      401(k) retirement plan
·      Paid holidays and PTO
·      Professional development and industry training
·      Career advancement opportunities within a growing company
·      Remote work flexibility

About AeroTech Mapping, Inc.

AeroTech Mapping is a leading provider of aerial mapping, LiDAR, land surveying, GIS, remote sensing, and geospatial solutions throughout the western United States. Since 2002, we have helped public agencies, engineering firms, utilities, and private clients make informed decisions through accurate geospatial data and innovative mapping technologies.

Ready to Build Your Future with AeroTech Mapping?

If you're looking for a career where your effort directly impacts your success, where you're trusted to manage your business, and where you can build lasting client relationships while representing industry-leading technology, we'd like to hear from you.

Qualified candidates are encouraged to apply early, as interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis.

Alicia Mendoza, PMP
Business Development Manager

Email: aliciamendoza@atmlv.com

jobs.title: Environmental Data Analyst - EOH Group
jobs.description:
ERG is a research and consulting firm that provides a wide range of support to federal, state, and commercial clients. ERG offers multidisciplinary teams with nationally recognized skills in engineering, science, economics, public health, informational technology, and communications. We hire people with the best minds and then provide them with a vibrant and flexible environment in which to develop their careers. The qualified individual must be highly motivated with the skills to prioritize, perform, and communicate effectively in a fast-paced environment. 

ERG’s Environmental and Occupational Health Group has an immediate opening for an early career professional to join our multi-disciplinary team. This individual will support a range of environmental and sustainability-related projects, including a clean energy grant program. The qualified individual must be highly motivated with the skills to prioritize, perform, and communicate effectively in a fast-paced environment. Responsibilities include managing large datasets, working with applicants to meet grant program requirements, using grant management software and related database applications to support client needs, and interfacing directly with clients.

Ideal candidates will have direct experience developing and supporting data visualization tools; conducting independent research and data analysis; and providing client services. 

Job Description:

Review clean energy grant applications for eligibility and completeness

Process payment requests and interface with applicants throughout the grant process

Identify and categorize potential application errors and communicate them to applicants and clients

Help develop and maintain a public-facing government data dashboard

Analyze, collect, and organize data to support greenhouse gas, energy, and water reduction projects, benchmarking, and reporting

Research and develop briefing materials on sustainability topics, including decarbonization and building and fleet electrification

Provide additional data analysis and technical communications support on environmental, sustainability, and public health topics

Qualifications and Skills:

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science or a related field

Minimum of one year of experience working with environmental or sustainability-related data

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other data management tools preferred

Experience with data visualization software, such as Microsoft Power BI, Tableau, or Qlik Sense

Familiarity with energy efficiency improvements, water conservation measures, and greenhouse gas emissions inventories

jobs.title: Environmental & Safety Professional
jobs.description:
Description

Leidos’ NISC IV Program (National Airspace System Integration Support Contract) is one of the largest and oldest programs supporting the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and we have an exciting career opportunity for an Environmental & Safety Professional to support the FAA with the goal of providing outstanding customer service to the Environmental Occupational Safety and Health (EOSH) Program.

In general, this person will be a part of a larger team of EOSH professionals that supports the FAA’s Eastern Service Area. The candidate will responsible for supporting many multi-faceted EOSH programs, and will be required to maintain applicable training and certification requirements as necessary. These programs include (but are not limited to) Asbestos, Lead, Mold, Chemical Management, Emergency Response, Electrical Safety, Water, Fuel Storage Tanks, and Fall Protection. The candidate will provide direct support to multi-level customers.

Remote with up to 50% travel. Report to customer site as needed.

Must be located in the Fayetteville or Raleigh/Durham, NC areas.

Specifically, the chosen candidate will have experience in writing reports with strict reporting deadlines. This includes extensive experience sampling and interpreting analytical reports and being able to identify exceedances in those reports. The selected candidate will also have experience climbing towers and/or be capable of receiving and giving fall protection training as well as completing tower safety inspections. The selected candidate must be able to provide comprehensive technical EOSH training to employees as requested. The selected candidate must have excellent customer service skills necessary to interact with senior level management and internal and external customers, as well as foster an environment of cooperation between different departments and co-workers. The chosen applicant must be a self-starter, able to work independently and with minimum supervision. This is a full time position that requires up to 75 percent travel. Overnight travel will be required in many instances. This position will be at the customer site in Memphis as requested.

Primary Responsibilities

Provide environmental and safety support to the FAA’s EOSH Programs. The primary programs are Indoor Air Quality (IAQ); Asbestos Management; Lead Management (paint); Polychlorinated Biphenyls Management; Chemical/Hazardous Waste Management; Pesticide Management; Drinking Water Management; Fuel Storage Tank Management; Fall Protection Program; Hearing Safety Program; Electrical Safety Program; Confined Space Program; and Radiation Program. Additionally, the candidate will be required to employ and be familiar with a wide variety of sampling instrumentation, sampling techniques.
Conduct site inspections and surveys, and submit proper technical reports conveying findings and sound guidance to resolve/mitigate any EOSH issues.
Manage inspections using electronic data; utilize on-line data storage locations; and be able to use all Microsoft programs.
Research and interpret Federal, State, Local, and FAA rules and regulations that are applicable to EOSH Programs.
Provide excellent problem-solving and customer service skills.

Basic Qualifications/Experience

Requires Bachelors degree and 2+ years of prior relevant experience or Masters degree and relevant experience.
Environmental, health and safety experience.
Proven experience with various types of EOSH field equipment (ex. PID, XRF, Dosimeter, etc.).
Proficient in obtaining and developing Asbestos samples & reports.
Experience in conducting and developing indoor air quality (IAQ) samples & reports.
Technical competence in surveying and developing Fall Protection issues & reports as well as Electrical Safety issues and reports.
Proficient in obtaining and developing Drinking Water samples and reports.
Must be strong in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and Microsoft Project.
Must be able to work, manage and maintain information stored in a Knowledge Sharing Network (KSN)/SharePoint site(s).
Candidate must also have a reliable vehicle.
Ability to obtain and maintain Public Trust Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Undergraduate Degree in Environmental Science, Occupational Safety & Health, or similar degree.
Master Degree in Occupational Safety & Health, Environmental Science or Environmental Engineering
Certified Safety Professional.
Certified Hazardous Materials Manager.

jobs.description:
Discover your full potential. At Tetra Tech, we are collaborating with industry-leading experts for a sustainable future for our world. We combine consulting and engineering with advanced analytics and technology to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our innovation hubs across the globe will enable you to share ideas and best practices while growing your professional network. Wherever you are in your career journey, you will benefit from working with world-class engineers, scientists, and technical specialists.

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Apply today and join the company that is Leading with Science®.

Tetra Tech is seeking a self-motivated, Entry-Level Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to support and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in air regulations, landfill gas systems, emissions compliance, and environmental data analysis.

In this role, you will support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing field and operational data, interpreting air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing compliance reports, and assisting with air permitting and emissions calculations. The primary focus areas include landfill gas monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas-to-Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Pollutants (NESHAP) regulations applicable to solid waste facilities.

This position is primarily remote, with limited, as-needed travel or occasional site visits. Only those in PST or MST will be considered.
Candidates must be comfortable working independently with limited supervision while collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.

This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT - paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $55K-$75K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. Only those that attach a cover letter will be considered.
The deadline to apply is 09/3/2026.

Your Role

Review, analyze, and interpret landfill air quality and landfill gas monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM, and air emissions datasets.
Compare monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit limits, and NSPS/NESHAP criteria to assess compliance.
Prepare environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
Support the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emission calculations and regulatory compliance demonstrations.
Collect, manage, track, and organize large datasets related to air emissions, landfill gas, SEM results, and compliance deadlines.
Develop and maintain templates, trackers, and tools to support consistent, accurate, and timely reporting for multiple facilities / landfills.
Coordinate with on-site operations, technicians, and subcontractors to confirm that monitoring, testing, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
Support Project Managers with deliverables, schedules, and client coordination including procurement of supplies, subcontractor coordination and Work Order development.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams on engineering, permitting, and environmental projects.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical and regulatory writing.
Proficiency in MS Office – specifically Word and Excel.
Ability to work independently in a remote environment, demonstrate initiative, and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with field staff, engineers, and regulatory agencies.
Valid driver’s license.
Ability and willingness to perform limited travel as required.
Interest and ability in developing technical and leadership skills within the Environmental Compliance field.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 25,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech
is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We invite applications from all interested parties.

Explore our open positions at https://www.tetratech.com/careers. Follow us on social media to learn more about our people, culture, and opportunities:

LinkedIn: @TetraTechCareers

X (Twitter): @TetraTechJobs

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

Please no phone calls or agencies.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Our Environmental group is looking for an Environmental Scientist
to join their team! As a graduate with this group, you will be engaged with projects that involve wetland delineations/assessments & permitting, endangered species surveys, water quality assessments, and ecological & environmental studies. These projects support ecological risk assessments, site characterization and remedial action projects on contaminated sites.

Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Wetland delineation

Ecological assessments to classify and map habitat cover types and plant communities
Surface water quality monitoring and sampling
Sediment sampling
Macroinverterate surveys / sampling
Fish, reptile and amphibian surveys
Managing and evaluating chemical and biological data
Evaluating and understanding environmental regulations
Preparing work plans, reports and other written communications

Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Biology, Ecology or related field of study
0-2 years of experience conducting wetland delineations and ecological field studies
Proficiency with managing and evaluating chemical and biological data using spreadsheets or database software
Familiarity with geographic information systems (GIS) applications software

jobs.description:
28800 Ida St Valley Nebraska 68064-8016

Why Valmont

We’re Here to Move the World Forward.

Valmont impacts millions of people around the world every day, yet they might not realize the many ways. Our technology is helping feed the growing population, supplying the world with more reliable energy and access to renewables, enhancing connectivity in remote and urban locations to create a sustainable future and so much more. Simply put, Valmont is advancing agricultural productivity and reimagining vital infrastructure to make life better.

Join a Fortune 1000 company that respects hard work, honors diversity and invests in our employees as we focus on creating the world of tomorrow, today. We are the modern workforce . Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.

A Brief Summary Of This Position

This position serves as Valmont’s Specialist, Environmental, Health & Safety, enabling overall company strategy in driving continuous improvement with EHS best practices across the organization. This position requires individual initiative on special projects to complete a wide variety of tasks that are part of Valmont’s comprehensive EHS initiatives. This includes participating in and facilitating the site level EHS teams and initiatives. The position will support implementation of Valmont’s EHS Playbook for the site. The Specialist, EHS facilitates the alignment of the site’s EHS activities with Valmont’s overall enterprise wide EHS strategies. The incumbent is responsible to swiftly detect sub-standard EHS performance using leading and lagging indicators and take action in conjunction with appropriate site and regional leadership teams. It is critical that the EHS Specialist assists others in their growth and knowledge in Safety, Health & Environmental practices. It is expected that the Specialist, EHS interacts with site production employees to identify and control hazards that can result in harm.

Essential Functions

Reports directly to the EHS Manager or General/Plant Manager, with matrixed reporting to the Regional Safety Manager and has no direct or indirect reports
Supports development, maintenance, and continuous improvement efforts to facilitate EHS strategic initiatives
Partners with regional and site management to ensure consistent deployment of standards, campaigns and initiatives across the organization
Supports the development and implementation of the site-specific annual EHS goals to measurably reduce risks and impacts.
Will learn and gain expertise in the company’s Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) information management system to manage data related to EHS events such as injuries, workers compensation claims, near miss incidents and internal and external inspections, and environmental permits
Assists in conducting the risk assessment process to recognize, evaluate, and control hazards throughout the site
Participates in and facilitates the deployment of environment, health and safety teams (e.g., Safety Committee, etc.) and facilitates their engagement in ownership of the activities required to maintain compliance, reduce the site’s environment footprint and drive continuous improvement
Assists the team based incident investigation process to help identify appropriate root cause and helps facilitate corrective action measures
Collects data for reporting and permit submittals for multi-media environmental regulatory requirements
Successful completion of the Valmont EHS Specialist curriculum within three months of hire

Other Important Details About The Role

Serves as a liaison between regional and site management, risk management and human resources on applicable topics
Assists in the development and implementation of emergency management and business continuity programs
Supports serious post incident reviews at their site, communication of incidents that result or have the potential to result in serious injury; partners with Regional EHS Directors/Managers and site representatives to identify root causes and preventive actions are effectively deployed across the organization
Assists with training/mentoring to regional/site representatives to strengthen EHS compliance and best practices
Formulates and implements actions on various EHS topics, as necessary, and shares updates with leadership
Facilitates the implementation of training programs to ensure regulatory compliance and incident best practices
Stay current with EHS property conservation regulations and standards
Demonstrates a commitment to the Valmont Core Values

Required Qualifications Of Every Candidate

Preferred Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree with 3 years of EHS or related experience, OR 5 years of experience of EHS or related experience
EHS responsibility with an emphasis on implementation and maintenance of environmental, health and safety programs, fire prevention, sustainability and risk management
Track record of making effective decisions, even when dealing with limited or ambiguous information
Ability to lead or support corporate, division, business unit and site teams responsible for managing EHS risks

Highly Qualified Candidates Will Also Possess These Qualifications

Previous experience with multi-national companies with progressive EHS programs
Experience with OSHA Voluntary Protection Programs (VPP) or ISO 45001, 14001 desired
Prior experience implementing and/or maintaining an enterprise-wide database system
Experience in a similar heavy manufacturing industry

Working Environment And Physical Efforts

The primary working conditions for this position is a manufacturing shop environment with exposure to dirt, grease, fumes, cold, heat, noise, dust. There will also be times when EHS Specialist works in an office environment. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses and hard hats may be required in most manufacturing areas and it is the EHS Specialist’s responsibility to ensure that all people (employees, vendors, customers, visitors) are in conformance with all safety requirements and that all employees are enforcing the safety requirements consistently and without exception. The incumbent is regularly required to sit for extended periods of time, as well as talk and listen on the phone and in personal conversations or meetings. Environment is fast paced and demanding most of the time. The employee frequently is required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms while working in the office with various files and forms and while working on the computer. The employee is occasionally required to move about the office. Incumbent must utilize proper ergonomic safeguards such as monitor height and positions, keyboard location and height and proper wrists rests. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 15 pounds in working with large files, binders, and computer equipment. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.

Benefits

Valmont offers employees and their families a comprehensive Total Wellbeing benefit package to ensure their individual and family’s overall wellness needs are met. Some offerings are dependent upon the role, work schedule, or location and can include the following:

Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)
401k retirement plan with company match
Paid time off
Employer paid life insurance
Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave
Work Life Support
Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 per year
Voluntary programs like tobacco cessation, Type 2 diabetes reversal, one-on-one health coaching, mortgage services and more

Valmont does not discriminate against any employee or applicant in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by law. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

If you have a disability and require any assistance in filling out the application for employment email EEOCompliance@Valmont.com.

jobs.description:
Overview

Wieland - Creating Value for Generations!

Wieland is a global leader in copper and copper alloy manufacturing, processing, and distribution. We provide a large product and service portfolio including power, automotive, ammunition, coinage, construction materials, refrigeration, electronics and many other industries. To us, metal is more than material.

Wieland's Cultural Values

Wieland’s culture is what makes for a fun and rewarding place to work! As a company, we benefit daily from our employees' knowledge and abilities. With our cultural vision, we place our core values at the heart of everything we do: safety
, ambition
, optimism
, reliability
, ownership
, diversity
, & respect
.

Wieland is hiring an Environmental Technician
. The Environmental/Wastewater Technician will be responsible for

the daily operation, monitoring, and optimization of the Wieland East Alton industrial wastewater treatment facility (WWTF). This position plays a critical role in ensuring compliance with environmental permits, regulatory requirements, and company environmental standards. In addition to wastewater treatment operations, the Environmental Technician supports site-wide environmental compliance through sampling, inspections, recordkeeping, data management, and other environmental program activities.

The successful candidate will be a self-motivated individual with strong technical aptitude, attention to detail, and a commitment to environmental stewardship, operational excellence, and workplace safety.

This role is located in East Alton, IL
and will be fully on-site.

Starting Pay:
$62,000-$75,000

Schedule:
Monday-Friday

Pay Schedule:
Bi-Weekly

Responsibilities

Environmental
Technician
Responsibilities:

Wastewater Treatment Plant Operations

Operate and monitor the WWTF to ensure effective treatment and permit compliance.
Perform routine system inspections of treatment equipment, pumps, tanks, piping systems, instrumentation, and controls.
Monitor treatment processes and adjust chemical feed rates, pH control systems, sludge handling equipment, and other operational parameters as needed.
Collect and analyze operational data to optimize treatment performance and identify potential issues.
Respond to alarms, process upsets, and equipment malfunctions and implement corrective actions.
Coordinate repairs with maintenance personnel and contractors.
Manage treatment chemicals and related inventories.
Maintain accurate operating logs, reports, and records required by operating permits and company procedures.
Assist in the preparation of regulatory reports and compliance documentation.

Environmental Sampling and Monitoring

Collect wastewater, stormwater, and other environmental samples in accordance with regulatory requirements and company procedures.
Coordinate laboratory analysis and maintain sample chain-of-custody documentation.
Review analytical data and communicate unusual results or trends to management.

Environmental Compliance Support

Conduct routine environmental inspections of site operations, storage areas, treatment systems, and waste management areas.
Support compliance activities associated with air permits, wastewater permits, stormwater permits, hazardous waste regulations, spill prevention programs, and other environmental requirements.
Assist with environmental audits and regulatory inspections.
Maintain environmental records, databases, and compliance tracking systems.
Participate in corrective action efforts and assist with implementation of compliance improvements.
Support environmental training initiatives as required.
Support implementation of corrective and preventive actions following environmental events.

General Responsibilities

Promote and maintain compliance with all company safety policies and procedures.
Maintain good housekeeping standards in environmental operating areas.
Work effectively with operations, maintenance, laboratory personnel, contractors, and regulatory agencies.
Perform other environmental and operational duties as assigned.

Environmental Technician
Qualifications:

High school diploma or GED required.
Minimum of 2 years of industrial wastewater treatment, water treatment, environmental compliance, or related industrial experience.
Working knowledge of environmental regulations and industrial wastewater treatment processes.
Ability to perform field sampling and environmental inspections.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to maintain accurate records and assist with preparation of technical reports.
Ability to obtain Illinois Wastewater Operator Class K license withing three months of employment.

Environmental Technician Preferred Qualifications
:

Associate degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Technology, Chemistry, Biology, Water Treatment, or a related technical field preferred.
Illinois Wastewater Operator Certification.
Experience operating industrial wastewater treatment systems in a manufacturing environment.
Experience with environmental permits, sampling programs, and regulatory compliance activities.
Familiarity with SCADA systems, PLC-controlled equipment, and process instrumentation.
Experience with hazardous waste management requirements.

Environmental Technician Physical Requirements:

Ability to work both indoors and outdoors in varied weather conditions.
Ability to walk long distances throughout an industrial facility.
Ability to climb stairs, ladders, and access elevated platforms.
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds.
Ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE).
Ability to work around treatment chemicals, moving equipment, and industrial processes safely.

Environmental Technician Work Environment:

Industrial manufacturing facility with exposure to noise, dust, heat, chemicals, and outdoor environmental conditions.
Occasional after-hours, weekends, or holiday work may be required to support plant operations, environmental monitoring, or emergency response activities.

Environmental Technician Key Performance Indicators:

Compliance with wastewater discharge permit limits.
Completion of required environmental sampling and inspections.
Timely and accurate regulatory reporting and recordkeeping.
Wastewater treatment plant operational reliability and uptime.
Successful completion of corrective actions identified during audits and inspections.
Safety performance and adherence to environmental compliance requirements.

Qualifications

Joining Wieland’s team gives you…

Benefits - Including Medical, Dental, Vision, Disability, Life & more!
Retirement Savings - 401(k) contribution + match.
Work/Life Balance - Paid Vacation & Holidays.
Growth Opportunities - We have over 9,000+ employees worldwide and 40+ locations in North America alone. Growth opportunities are limitless!
Wellness Programs - Wieland encourages participation in our unique and personalized approach to wellness, where you are eligible to earn healthcare premium discounts as well as HSA employer contributions based on your status within the program.
Sustainability - Wieland continues to break ground with eco-friendly solutions and push the barrier in sustainability for future generations.

Wieland is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer
. We celebrate diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive environment for all employees. Come join Wieland today and help us continue to build a global corporation we are all proud to belong to.

jobs.title: Conservation Director
jobs.description:
Want to make a positive difference to the future of people and our one shared home, the Earth? Working at WWF could be your opportunity of a lifetime.

All around the world, people are waking up to the devastating impacts of climate change and nature loss. The situation today is worse than the darkest predictions of just ten years ago, pushing billions of people to the edge and threatening lives and livelihoods. At WWF, we are facing our biggest crisis – and our biggest ever opportunity – to create a better future for people and nature. With over 60 years of experience and an active presence in more than 100 countries, we work to achieve both on-the-ground and global policy action, from protecting and restoring species and their habitats, to transforming markets and policies toward sustainability.

Our people come from hugely diverse backgrounds and with a variety of expertise, ranging from conservation science and advocacy to HR and finance. We welcome applications from anyone who believes they can help us tackle this enormous global challenge and drive the urgent conservation impact needed to restore our planet.

What We Do

We are an independent conservation organization, striving to sustain the natural world for the benefit of people and the ecosystem. From individuals and communities to businesses and governments, we are part of a growing global movement calling for bolder action on climate and nature, demanding that world leaders set nature on the path to recovery by 2030. WWF works to address the most dominant drivers of nature loss through system-wide changes in how food and energy are produced and consumed, and in how financial systems are structured. By implementing change in every country, we aim to drive visible and positive impacts on the ground, helping to restore nature in the most critical places around the world, from the Amazon to the Coral Triangle.

Engaging everyone means addressing the barriers to participation faced by some groups in society, including local communities. Conservation will only be sustainable if it is owned by, and benefits, local people. That’s why Indigenous Peoples and local communities must be at the centre of action on climate and nature. WWF is committed to using its resources and global network to support these communities in creating together the most effective solutions where they live.

Humanity is still in time, we have a clear pathway to solve this crisis. At WWF, we call on everyone to join the global movement, change how we live, and take action now.

Background

WWF Caucasus Programme Office (WWF CauPO) is the leading international conservation organisation in the South Caucasus, operating in Georgia (regional hub), Armenia and Azerbaijan. It represents a highly performing WWF international Programme Office with efficient operating systems, professional and skilled staff, strong financial resources, delivering high conservation impact. WWF CauPO is guided by strong conservation vision for the region. The role of the Conservation Department is to ensure the effective implementation of conservation strategies and initiatives for the region and consistent strong impact measurement, reflection and learning from results to continuously improve performance.

Major Function

The WWF Caucasus, Conservation Director sets strategic conservation and policy directions for the region and supervises their performance through robust PMEL frameworks and relevant indicators. Directs conservation program initiatives on a regional level to ensure coherent/ cohesive programme design and delivery and guides conservation planning and implementation in each Caucasus country. Leads on partner development and stakeholder engagement in Georgia, for policy influence, conservation delivery and fundraising purposes. Provides strategic leadership to the conservation teams and consultants engaged in project implementation across all three countries.

Major Duties And Responsibilities

Strategic Conservation Leadership

Serve on the Regional Management Team (RMT), contributing to region-wide policies, systems, and standards.
Maintain strong coordination with RMT members to align activities with WWF CauPO objectives.
Lead strategic conservation planning processes with the Conservation Managers in CauPo’s offices, ensuring a current, coherent WWF CauPO Conservation Plan aligned with regional and WWF Network priorities.
Oversee review, updates, and implementation of the WWF CauPO conservation strategy and associated policies, systems, and procedures.
Lead the Conservation team in the development, submission, and monitoring of funding proposals to ensure alignment with strategic forecasts and conservation priorities.
Oversee effective monitoring, evaluation, and reporting of the WWF CauPO Conservation Plan, ensuring compliance with WWF standards, KPIs, and GPF indicators.

ESSF
, Quality Assurance and Risk Management

Develop and maintain WWF CauPO’s quality assurance systems to ensure conservation relevance and programmatic integrity across all proposals and initiatives
Supervise implementation and updates of Environmental & Social Safeguards (ESSF) across landscapes and projects, including risk screening, training, and reporting.
Guide the integration of ESSF and risk management measures into conservation planning and project design.
Ensure that programmatic risks are identified, tracked in the risk register, and effectively mitigated and evaluate project proposals for strategic relevance and quality, supporting a strong internal quality assurance system.
Stay abreast of WWF International QA and ESSF policy developments and ensure institutional alignment and capacity.

Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL)

Design and oversee M&E strategy and frameworks that align with organisational goals, donor expectations, and international standards.
Lead development and use of logframes, theories of change, KPIs, and data systems for tracking conservation impact.
Ensure timely data analysis, impact assessment, and integration of findings into adaptive program management.
Build MEL capacity across the region, guiding staff and partners on best practices, tools, and reporting.

Team Management and Talent Development

Supervise and mentor conservation staff across the region, supporting performance, motivation, and professional development.
Oversee the work of three conservation managers in the three CauPO offices
Collaborate with RMT and P&C on workforce planning, recruitment, succession planning, and talent development for the conservation function.
Support recruitment and evaluation of key conservation and programme staff, including consultants as needed.

Communications, Partnerships & Representation

Act as spokesperson for the WWF CauPO Conservation Programme to the WWF Network and internal fora such as Conservation Leadership Community and European Directors Community, media, partners, and external stakeholders.
Contribute to communications products and campaigns that promote WWF CauPO’s image and impact.
Foster partnerships and represent WWF CauPO in relevant regional and global forums.

Fundraising and donor relationship management

Lead proposal development in close cooperation with Network colleagues, donors, and external agencies to secure relevant funding for the WWF Caucasus strategy
Ensure alignment of project delivery with donor expectations, and ensure timely monitoring and quality reporting
Actively develop project pipeline to support future income generation and effective cost recovery
Build and maintain relationships with donors, agencies and partners in support of fundraising efforts from diverse channels.

Profile

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree or higher in natural resources management, environmental or conservation management, development studies, or in relevant fields.
At least 10 years of practical experience in leading and managing integrated conservation programme at regional level.
Demonstrated experience in developing, implementing and monitoring strategic plans.
Thorough understanding of conservation and development issues in the region.
Knowledge of the policy/institutional context related to conservation in region.
Experience in developing and writing related project proposals to aid agencies, foundations, corporate sector and other individual donors.
Excellent understanding of development partnerships, fundraising, donor strategies, functions, governmental and international relations.
Strong oral and written communication skills in English, Russian and Georgian languages.

Required Skills And Competencies

Strategic thinking and decision making.
Excellent communication, negotiation and diplomatic skills.
Ability to relate convincingly and credibly with diverse audiences.
Strong organizational skills with an aptitude to get things done.
Leadership and management, People management, Coaching and capacity building/development.
Policy advocacy and influence.
Management of conflict, risk, and crisis.
Promoting team synergy in a multi-cultural work environment.
Identifies and aligns with the core values of the WWF organization: Courage, Collaboration, Respect & Integrity.
Adheres to WWF’s brand values: Knowledgeable, Optimistic, Determined and Engaging.
Demonstrates WWF behaviours in ways of working: strive for impact, listen deeply, collaborate openly and innovate fearlessly.

Working Relationships

Internal:
Interacts extensively with other departments at WWF Caucasus Programme Office, WWF Armenia and WWF Azerbaijan Country Offices, EUNA Regional Conservation Director as well as WWF International, National Organizations and Country Offices throughout the Network.

External:
Interacts with relevant Governmental institutions, business sector, academia, NGO sector, local communities and donors.

This job description covers the main tasks and conveys the spirit of the sort of tasks anticipated proactively from staff. Other tasks may be assigned as necessary according to organizational needs.

WWF is an equal opportunity employer and committed to having a diverse workforce.

Please upload your covering letter and CV in English. Priority will be given to applications with both documents indicated.

Deadline for applications: 14 th September, 2025

Work permit restrictions may apply.

Early application is encouraged as we will review applications throughout the advertising period and reserve the right to close the advert early.

At WWF, we are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace where every individual feels valued and respected. We believe that a diverse workforce will help us to achieve our mission to stop the degradation of the Earth's natural environment and to build a future in which humans live in harmony with nature. As an equal opportunity employer, we are committed to providing fair and unbiased consideration for all candidates regardless of their background. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply and join us in fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.

jobs.description:
Company: United Water Restoration Group

Job Type: Full Time

Location: Jacksonville

The Largest privately owned restoration company in the State of Florida is looking for its newest Remediation Technician who are looking to take the next step in their career. United Water Restoration Group has locations throughout the state and they are all growing, so we’re looking for experienced, talented and motivated individuals ready to take on their next challenge. We strive to bring the best technicians in the industry because that’s what our customers deserve. Let’s turn the worst experiences of their life into one of the best. And that starts with you!

United Water Restoration offers a competitive hourly rate ($20 - $22 per hour, based on experience for Restoration Technicians) and a comprehensive benefits package that includes health insurance plans (medical, dental, and vision), a 401(k) plan with guaranteed match, 6 paid holidays, and Paid Vacation time. Listen to what your new coworkers have to say about working at United Water Restoration in our testimonial video here.

The Restoration Technician is a first responder to property loss situations and helps to mitigate the damage in both residential and commercial structures. Technicians are responsible for water damage mitigation, structural board-up and security, on-location cleaning, and microbial remediation.

Principal Duties & Responsibilities

Water extraction and mitigation
Fire and smoke cleaning and restoration
Microbial remediation
Vandalism, crime scene, and biohazard clean up
Demolition
Structural board-up and site stabilization
On-location cleaning
Equipment set up, monitoring, and break down
Field management and supervision of all temporary labor personnel
Manage and maintain a clean and organized appearance of the vehicle, equipment, material, and consumables on the job site and warehouse at all times
Manage and maintain inventories of all equipment, material, consumables, and tools
Representation on UWRG Emergency Mitigation On-Call Rotation
Complete all necessary paperwork including daily progress reports, moisture logs, safety logs, and diagrams
Provide the highest level of customer service
Adheres to all company best practices.
All other duties or projects as assigned.

Qualifications/Experience

Restoration industry experience (water, fire, and mold) is required
IICRC accreditations for fire & smoke, water damage, and microbial remediation are preferred. If you’re not certified, we’ll get you there.
Excellent communicator, both verbally and written
Ability to work with people in a professional manner
Maintains a valid and current driver’s license
Successfully pass a national criminal background check and motor vehicle report background check
Successfully pass a pre-employment drug screening

Work Environment and Physical Demands for Position
